description: Read-only demonstration projection of existing GitView specifications; source YAML is authoritative. Not an independently authored candidate graph.

nodes.title: GitView - product intent and scope
nodes.description: Give a person managing many GitHub repositories a compact native iOS overview of current PR and Issue work, including work produced by coding agents, attention and outcomes, with a path to the original GitHub objects.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The operator can survey Projects and their GitHub repository work, identify attention and supported outcomes, and reach the original GitHub objects.
Projects contain one or more repositories and can share a repository; repository identity and Project membership survive a source-confirmed rename or transfer.

Today presents older unfinished work and work completed in the current local calendar day, including merged or closed objects unless applicable persistent filters hide them; an object remains one object when its state changes.
The overview supports discrete zoom and accessible inspection, including first-version long-press preview and explicit opening, while retaining valid Project and selection context.
PR review, CI, discussion and lifecycle remain distinct, with merged PRs represented as the primary Done outcome and readiness to merge a separate signal whose predicate remains to be defined.

Historical Project graphs use current repository membership, disclose missing evidence, and do not portray unknown history as zero; the envisaged calendar shows daily work intensity rather than CI health.

Locally stored supported observations remain distinguishable from current source facts; refresh failure is visible and confirmed private Repository revocation follows the selected retained-data and account-switch boundaries.

The product scope preserves system appearance, accessibility, lightweight source sharing and the selected engineering directions without declaring an implementation or implementation-ready descendants.

nodes.title: GitView - Repository identity across rename and transfer
nodes.description: Preserve the identity and context of a GitHub Repository as its name or owner changes.

requirements.statement: When GitHub confirms that a renamed or transferred repository is the same source object, GitView keeps one Repository with its existing history and all Project memberships. A change of owner does not itself rename a Project or create another Repository.
A repository name, owner or address may change and alone does not establish identity. When a changed address is confirmed to be current, GitView updates the supported current source address.

Within one GitHub instance, compare confirmed numeric REST repository IDs under the selected ontology policy: the same ID identifies the same Repository, while a different ID identifies a different Repository even at a reused address. The owner approved the recorded same/different numeric examples, and later approved the ontology containing the REST mapping; those are distinct decisions. An ID match alone does not prove that a transfer happened.
If GitHub confirms that an object at a previously used address is a different repository, it does not inherit the earlier Repository's history or Project memberships merely through that address.

An unavailable, incomplete or ambiguous observation does not establish identity, deletion or loss of Project membership. Keep last supported information and represent uncertainty until evidence permits reconciliation; the access policy governs whether retained data can be shown.
Preserving existing history does not promise that GitView possesses a complete source history or can recover information that was never available.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Source-confirmed rename or transfer preserves one Repository, its existing history and every Project membership.
Reuse of an address by a source-confirmed different repository does not transfer history or memberships.
An unavailable or ambiguous observation remains uncertain and does not alone establish deletion or identity.

The same-instance numeric REST repository ID comparison selected in the approved ontology, the owner-accepted numeric examples and the 404 outcome are distinguishable from unverified source observations and an implementation.

nodes.title: GitView - Stored observations and refresh
nodes.description: Reuse previously received data while keeping refresh outcomes, freshness and incomplete coverage understandable.

requirements.statement: Store accepted observations for reuse across launches; storage failure and actual recoverability do not imply unconditional preservation. When stored observations are recoverable and eligible for display, make them available without waiting for a new GitHub request; apply the applicable access policy.

Apply accepted successful observations to the facts and scope they support. Record and present the supported scope and time of a successful observation separately from refresh attempt outcomes. Updating repository metadata does not itself update the PR or Issue list or its last successful time.

A failed refresh visibly identifies the affected scope and GitHub failure and shows its last supported successful observation time when known and permitted. Retain eligible last-known data without presenting it as newly refreshed. No successful observation is distinct from a confirmed empty result; do not invent a success time.

For a private Repository with source-confirmed access revocation, follow 0019 and retain already saved local observations. While its account remains active, show them with the revocation indication and supported last update time when known; stop synchronization while revocation applies. Do not treat a transient failure or a 404 alone as proof of revocation or as proof of successful refresh.

A partial response or interrupted retrieval retains actual observation context and incomplete coverage. A partial observation has its own time and does not advance the last complete successful observation time of the requested scope or establish complete coverage. Failure alone does not erase accepted data, establish deletion or turn unknown work into a confirmed empty collection. Explicit clearing, independent accepted updates and access changes retain their own effects.
On opening with stale data, request an update of the applicable scope subject to available API budget. Exact staleness and ordering policy remain open.
Request background refresh opportunities; iOS controls whether and when execution is granted. Do not promise a fixed frequency, and keep work bounded by the granted opportunity.
Offer pull-to-refresh where appropriate to the screen or an equivalent explicit refresh action. Manual requests follow applicable source limits and show their own result.

Account for shared applicable GitHub rate limits across manual, foreground and background work, query cost and partial retrieval; avoid flooding. When source-directed retry or reset constraints apply, avoid retrying before they permit it. Exact request sizes, concurrency, pagination, retry scheduling and REST or GraphQL choices require later refinement.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Eligible last-known data can be used without waiting for a new request, subject to applicable access restrictions.
Refresh failure and last supported successful time are distinguishable for the affected scope when known.
Partial coverage remains visible as incomplete whether the supported selection is empty or nonempty; its observation time does not establish a fully refreshed scope.
Partial, failed or never-observed data is not silently represented as a complete empty result.
Manual and stale-on-open refresh and system-granted background opportunities respect applicable source limits.

Previously accepted observations are stored locally for subsequent use across launches, subject to applicable access policy; failed storage or uncertain recovery is not presented as successful preservation.

nodes.title: GitView - Main overview
nodes.description: Let the operator quickly survey Projects, see where work is progressing or needs attention, and open the relevant work.

requirements.statement: Provide an overview of saved GitView Projects whose representation is permitted, identifiable where their information is permitted, with available work and attention signals inspectable. Project means a user-defined collection of Repositories, not a GitHub organization.
Preserve the actual scope, unit, observation and coverage of Project summaries under 0047; do not silently add overlapping Project totals as unique portfolio totals.

The operator can open a selected Project and use actionable Project signals to reach corresponding scoped work under 0006. The Today work selection follows 0007; ordinary entry to a multi-Repository Project opens its Project-wide work grid, and its Repository list is available in Project settings. Today is the opening current-work mode, not a decision that the work grid must be the first app screen; cold-launch navigation remains open.

Distinguish confirmed empty local Project collection from incomplete or unobserved data, stale results and refresh failure. A failed refresh retains eligible prior observations and exposes scoped failure and supported observation time according to 0003; missing data is not confirmed absence.

Use the selected Photos-inspired grid with pinch and multiple density levels within a scope under 0014, and Apple system look, with accessible alternatives to gestures and color-only distinctions. Exact density, controls and how details fit at different scales require refinement.

Changing density and opening or returning from an object retain valid Project, selection and permitted source context; do not silently switch to an unrelated Project when the original cannot be established.

When GitHub confirms access revocation for a private Repository, keep its saved Project and available local information for the affected Repository visible as last known with the revocation indication and supported update time when known. Stop synchronization for the affected Repository and retain a discoverable path to access recovery or explicit local deletion under 0019. Other account-change disclosure cases remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Permitted Projects are identifiable and their available work and attention are inspectable.
Project and actionable-signal navigation preserve applicable scope and source context.
An unobserved or failed source refresh does not become a confirmed empty Project or an invented success time.
The overview remains operable without reliance on color or a single gesture.

Confirmed private Repository revocation keeps the saved Project and available local information for the affected Repository visible with its indication and supported time when known, and preserves recovery or explicit local deletion under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Project composition and membership
nodes.description: Let the operator organize GitHub repositories into identifiable GitView Projects for work overview.

requirements.statement: A saved Project has a stable local identity, a name, an optional description and one or more source-identified GitHub repositories. A Project and its repositories remain distinct objects.
A repository may belong to more than one Project. Repositories from different GitHub organizations may belong to the same Project; organization is source metadata, not the Project boundary.

By default there is one Project per repository. Persistent association with reuse is an agent-authored working candidate, not a selected owner requirement; its recovery protocol and alternative mechanisms require separate refinement.

The operator can create, rename and edit a Project and select its repositories. Removing membership from one Project does not delete the source repository or alter membership in another Project. A saved Project must not become an invalid empty Project; exact editing and recovery interaction require refinement.

When the source confirms the same GitHub repository after rename or transfer, its identity, history and Project memberships are preserved. A name or address alone is not sufficient to identify a repository.

An unavailable observation or uncertain save outcome does not prove a repository, Project or membership absent. Distinguish an operation outcome from the last supported configuration and reconcile when evidence permits; otherwise retain the uncertainty without silently duplicating a still-possible previous effect. Recovery is not guaranteed when necessary evidence is unavailable.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A Project with one or more confirmed repositories is distinguishable from each repository and from GitHub organizations.
A repository can participate in two Projects, including one that contains repositories from multiple organizations.
A valid membership change affects its selected Project without changing GitHub or another Project's membership.
The default of one Project per Repository is distinguished from the persistent-association mechanism not selected by the owner.
Unknown identity, unavailable configuration and an indeterminate save do not become a confirmed absence or safe duplicate.

nodes.title: GitView - Project contents and navigation
nodes.description: Let the operator navigate from a Project overview to its repositories and their work while retaining context.

requirements.statement: Project and Repository remain distinct and identifiable in the permitted context. Repository membership follows its identity rather than its current organization, owner or name. One Repository in two Projects retains the context of the Project from which it was opened.

For a Project with several Repositories, ordinary Project entry opens one Project-wide PR and Issue grid spanning the applicable member scope. The list of member Repositories is available in Project settings. The operator can inspect permitted members and reach each member’s work; the exact navigation route remains open. Repositories from different GitHub organizations remain within the same Project; restricted information follows the applicable access policy.
For a Project containing one Repository, reach its work without a redundant intermediate Repository screen. Preserve the distinction and permitted source context of both Project and Repository.

A selectable Project summary signal offers direct access to its corresponding work selection across the applicable member scope without first traversing individual Repositories. Show each object's source Repository where permitted, and retain the origin signal or filter and its scope. Selection semantics, metric computation and evidence require separate refinement.

Density changes within the same scope do not silently change Project, Repository scope, applicable time period or filters. When returning from an object, preserve the valid originating context, applicable period, filter and scale, and restore position where possible; if the origin is no longer valid or cannot be verified, do not silently present a different scope as the original.

Incomplete or unavailable observations do not establish an empty Repository, remove a Project member, or prove that a signal selection is exhaustive. Convey applicable coverage limitations without disclosing restricted data.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A single-Repository Project reaches its work without a redundant intermediate Repository screen and retains both identities.
A multi-Repository Project provides permitted member inspection and routes to each member's work.
A selectable Project signal reaches its corresponding work across the applicable Project scope without a Repository-by-Repository detour.
Density and return navigation preserve supported context without silently switching scope.
Incomplete source observations are not represented as a confirmed empty member or exhaustive selection.
Ordinary entry to a multi-Repository Project opens its Project-wide work grid; the member list is available in Project settings.

nodes.title: GitView - Today work grid and lifecycle filters
nodes.description: Let the operator see current work and today's completed work together in a compact Project grid and narrow it explicitly.

requirements.statement: Today provides an overview of applicable PRs and Issues in the selected Project and their source Repository context. Membership and access eligibility remain subject to their respective contracts.

Unfinished work remains eligible even if it began on an earlier day. Work completed during the current calendar day remains eligible. The day uses the user's local time zone. Completion on the previous day alone does not qualify an object for the new Today; other applicable conditions may do so.

Each source-confirmed PR or Issue has one cell in a selection, even if several inclusion conditions apply. A linked PR and Issue are distinct objects; equal issue or PR numbers in different repositories do not establish identity. Unresolved identity is not presented as confirmed uniqueness.

Without an applicable saved exclusion, eligible objects are shown in all lifecycle states, including merged and closed. A PR merged today updates the same cell and remains in unfiltered Today; it leaves an unfinished-only selection. Closed without merge is not called merged.

The operator can explicitly hide applicable states, including merged and closed. Selected filters persist between launches and are restored when applicable; failed or unknown persistence is not reported as a confirmed save. Filters narrow the view rather than changing source objects. When opening a signal originating inside this filtered selection, retain its applicable filter context under 0092; a signal outside it follows its own origin context.

Incomplete or failed refresh, missing pages or unknown status do not prove a merge, deletion or empty selection. Last supported permitted observations retain their freshness and access limitations; an unfiltered grid is not proof of complete GitHub coverage.

The owner envisages zooming out further from Today to reach a calendar of daily work intensity for the applicable selected Project scope under 0018. Calendar inclusion in the first version and exact interaction remain unselected.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Earlier unfinished work and work completed on the current local calendar day remain eligible in Today.
A change of lifecycle state updates the same object's cell; a linked PR and Issue remain distinct.
All applicable lifecycle states are visible without saved exclusions, and explicit lifecycle filters persist across launches.
A previous day's completion alone does not qualify an object for the new Today.
Incomplete source observations do not become confirmed success, deletion or an exhaustive empty result.

nodes.title: GitView - Pull request overview
nodes.description: Provide a compact, source-linked overview of a selected PR and its independently meaningful signals.

requirements.statement: Show supported permitted source identity, repository-local number, title, description and GitHub link, retaining the correct Repository context. An unavailable source link must not be replaced with another object.
Distinguish open, closed without merge and merged from the draft flag, labels, review and CI. Show supported labels when available and permitted.

Show the supported permitted target Repository, source and target branches, observed revision, author, requested reviewers and related Issues. Keep the supported PR-associated Repository distinct from separately supported base or target and head or source Repository contexts; an unavailable context remains unknown rather than being inferred from another. This does not require a separate head Repository field in the overview. A related Issue does not itself prove an actor’s motive.

Show supported source review assessment and separate counts of total and unresolved review threads. Individual thread content is outside the selected overview; unavailable counts or assessment are not zero or approval. Where supported, distinguish unavailable assessment, absence of reviews, and a source-reported requirement for review; do not infer one from another.

Show supported counts for red, yellow, green and total current individual PR checks, following GitHub's general behavior. Do not count prior retries as additional current checks; precise mappings, revision selection and special outcomes require validation. The three color counts are not presumed to sum to total.
Show supported additions and deletions separately, changed-file count and commit count; these are counts, not an in-app diff, file, commit or run browser.
Distinguish source creation, update, closure or merge times from observation time and source when available.

Preserve permitted authored text and the selected Problem, Motivation, Expected outcome, Changes, Validation and References format where present. Authored Validation is not proof of current CI status.
Provide a route to the original GitHub object and lightweight sharing when an eligible link is available.
Unavailable or stale facts retain their limitations and access context; do not infer success, zero or identity.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The selected PR retains its identity and source Repository context, with supported permitted identifying fields.
The supported permitted target Repository is inspectable; supported PR-associated and base or head Repository contexts remain distinguishable, and an unavailable context is not invented.
Lifecycle, draft, review assessment, thread counts, check counts and change counts remain distinct and unknown values are not zero.
The overview offers the source route when an eligible link is available and indicates unavailability otherwise; authored description remains separate from observed CI.
The selected scope does not require in-app diff, individual thread, file, commit or run details.

nodes.title: GitView - Issue overview
nodes.description: Provide a compact, source-linked overview of a selected Issue and its supported relationships.

requirements.statement: Show supported permitted source identity, repository-local number, title, description and GitHub link while retaining the correct Repository context. Do not substitute another object for an unavailable link.
Distinguish open and closed, source-provided state or closure reason, labels and type. Closed does not automatically mean completed, and an unavailable reason remains unknown.
Show supported source Repository, author, assignees and milestone without inferring that an assignee has begun work.

Show supported linked PRs, parent and direct sub-issues, and dependencies in each direction. Distinguish a supported closing reference from a mention; the same PR can have both meanings. A link alone does not establish a completed outcome or an actor's motive, and incomplete relationship evidence is not a confirmed absence.
When the same source-confirmed PR has both supported link meanings, identify it once in its Repository context while retaining both the mention and the closing-reference meanings.

Show supported comment and participant counts, and total and closed direct-sub-issue counts separately. These do not establish percent complete; individual comments are outside the selected overview. Unknown counts are not zero.
Distinguish creation, update, closure, observation and last-comment times, and observation source when available.
Preserve permitted authored text and the selected Problem, Motivation, Expected outcome and References format where present; source text and separately supported relationships retain their meanings.
Provide a route to the original GitHub object and lightweight sharing when an eligible link is available.
Unavailable or stale facts retain their limitations and access context; do not infer successful completion or absence.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The selected Issue retains its identity and Repository context with supported permitted identifying fields and state reason.
A closing reference and mention remain distinct supported meanings; a link does not establish motive.
Relationship directions and selected count units remain distinct, and unknowns are not presented as zeros or completion.
The overview offers the source route when an eligible link is available and indicates unavailability otherwise; the selected description remains as authored where available.

nodes.title: GitView - Issue and PR description formats
nodes.description: Preserve authored Issue and PR descriptions while supporting the selected structured formats.

requirements.statement: Issue descriptions use Problem, Motivation, Expected outcome and References.
PR descriptions use Problem, Motivation, Expected outcome, Changes, Validation and References.

Require the agreed sections in new Issue and PR descriptions through the participating repository process and cover its supported creation paths. Provide the agreed templates for that process; templates and agent instructions alone are not evidence of enforcement.

Existing or external objects with another format or missing sections remain visible when eligible for display under the access policy in 0019; format alone does not hide them. Preserve their authored text, indicate a confirmed missing section and do not invent material or silently discard nonconforming objects.

Motivation, Expected outcome and Validation are authored statements. A linked Issue is not proof of a specific actor's motive; declared outcome is not proof it happened; declared validation is distinct from observed CI and independent test evidence. Preserve attribution of authored text and the meaning of independently supported source links when available, without inferring an actor's motive or causation.
When a section cannot reliably be extracted, retain the original permitted text instead of inventing structured content.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The selected Issue and PR formats retain their distinct named sections and apply to new descriptions through all supported creation paths of the participating process; the templates support but do not prove enforcement.
Eligible external or legacy descriptions remain visible under the access policy in 0019; format alone does not hide them, fabricate sections or silently discard original text.
Authored motivation, outcomes and validation are distinguishable from independently established facts and CI.

nodes.title: GitView - Current checks and review signals
nodes.description: Keep current PR check counts, review assessments and thread counts independently interpretable.

requirements.statement: Show supported counts of current individual PR checks as red, yellow, green and total, retaining applicable revision, observation and coverage. A workflow run or historical attempt is not automatically another current check. When the current check set or revision cannot be established, report the limitation rather than a complete count.

Special or unknown outcomes remain distinguishable until a supported mapping exists. Do not assume red, yellow and green sum to total, or that an absent, pending or unknown check result is successful.

Show supported permitted source review assessment and both total and unresolved thread counts; a review request remains independently meaningful. Where evidence supports it, distinguish an unavailable assessment, absence of reviews and a source-reported review requirement. Preserve each fact's context and do not infer one from another signal.

A CI color, review assessment, zero visible threads or single glyph alone does not establish merge readiness. A complete zero-check result is distinct from unobserved checks and is not automatically merge-ready.
Facts from an earlier revision remain associated with that observation; do not silently present an old approval or check outcome as current for a newly observed revision without applicable evidence.
These are counts and summary signals; the selected PR overview does not require in-app thread content or run details.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Supported permitted review assessment and both thread counts are shown; unavailable assessment, absence of reviews and source-reported review requirement remain distinct when supported.
Current check counts retain supported revision and coverage; old attempts are not counted as new current checks without evidence.
Review assessment, review request and thread counts remain independent; unknown or pending is not a confirmed success.
Confirmed zero checks is distinguishable from unobserved checks and does not by itself establish merge readiness.

nodes.title: GitView - Repository and Project summaries
nodes.description: Make current work, attention and outcomes interpretable at Repository and Project scopes.

requirements.statement: A Repository work summary makes supported permitted open PR counts, draft subset and open Issue counts distinguishable, with applicable CI, review, unresolved-thread and blocked-Issue attention. Its current facts retain source scope, coverage and freshness; each supported distinct source-confirmed identity is counted once within each applicable identity-based Repository measurement, even when observed on multiple pages; one PR may still contribute to different overlapping signals.

A Project summary covers its applicable member Repositories under 0047, including a Repository also present in another Project. Restrictions and incomplete member observations affect what can be disclosed or asserted as complete.

Distinguish affected PRs from individual failed checks and affected Repositories. Attention categories may overlap; do not add them as independent problems. A linked PR and Issue are separate source objects, not automatically separate tasks.

Distinguish merged PRs and closed Issues by supported reason for a selected period from current-state counts. Keep scope, observation context and incomplete evidence visible; closure alone does not establish completion. For PRs, the primary «Done» indicator refers to merged PRs; readiness to merge is a separate desired signal whose applicable predicate and evidence remain open.

An actionable signal retains its actual condition and scope when opening the corresponding permitted object selection. A count of checks, threads or events is not automatically the number of resulting object cards.

When a unique portfolio-wide count is asserted, count confirmed Repository and object identities once, even if a Repository belongs to multiple Projects. This does not remove its contribution from each applicable Project summary.
A checks-and-review-passed selection is conditional on a separately accepted applicable predicate and is not a guarantee of merge readiness. Do not fabricate it from missing observations.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Supported current work and attention retain their Repository or Project scope, units, coverage and freshness.
Project membership overlap and any claimed unique portfolio count follow confirmed identities without double counting.
Overlapping attention signals and different units are not added as independent tasks or substituted for object-card counts.
Period outcomes remain distinct from current-state counts and unavailable coverage is not presented as confirmed zero.

nodes.title: GitView - Metrics, history and charts
nodes.description: Make work and completion trends interpretable without inventing historical observations.

requirements.statement: A measurement identifies its subject, unit, scope, period, source and coverage as applicable. Distinguish current-state snapshots from historical events and keep observation time separate from event time.

Show supported permitted current open PR and open Issue counts separately with their coverage; draft PRs are a subset of open PRs. Linked PRs and Issues are distinct source objects but are not automatically independent tasks.

With sufficient supported evidence, show merged PR and closed Issue outcomes separately for an identified period; preserve supported Issue closure reasons and unknowns. Closed does not automatically mean completed. For PRs, the primary «Done» indicator means merged PRs; readiness to merge is a separate desired signal, not another name for the merged outcome.

Show graphs of applicable summary measurements when sufficient history exists. A missing historical value remains a gap or explicitly incomplete, not a zero or a current snapshot backfilled as past history.

Recalculate a Project's historical graph over the selected period using the Project's current Repository membership. Adding a Repository can include its supported earlier activity; removing it excludes its contribution on subsequent recalculation. Identify the actual membership basis and do not present it as the Project's historical membership. Access, evidence and coverage still apply; an unavailable earlier contribution is not zero and a partial result is not complete.

A later permitted source observation may support an earlier event with its real event and observation times, but one known event does not prove complete period coverage or reconstruct an earlier current-state population.
Support understanding of unfinished work and completion; do not claim a defined burn-down formula, fixed cohort or independent-task total until separately specified.

Each value preserves applicable scope, access, freshness and coverage. Mixed observation times or missing data do not become a complete simultaneous snapshot, a successful observation or a confirmed zero.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Historical Project graphs use the current Repository membership basis and do not claim it is historical Project membership.
Current work and period outcomes retain distinct subjects, units, scopes and applicable observation contexts.
PR and Issue counts or series are not represented as independent tasks merely because the objects differ.
Insufficient historical evidence remains a gap or explicitly incomplete rather than a fabricated zero.
A later-observed event retains its event and observation times and does not prove complete historical coverage.
Formal burn-down semantics are not assumed by this overview.

nodes.title: GitView - Zoomable grid
nodes.description: Provide a Photos-inspired grid that moves between dense overview and more detailed cards within a stable scope.

requirements.statement: Pinch increases or decreases grid detail through discrete density levels. Within a level and before its boundary, changes preserve the current scope, selected period, filters and selected objects. When an expanding cell reaches its maximum size, the gesture triggers a transition to the corresponding next level; the maximum depends on grid width and the chosen maximum cell size in points.

Source observations or membership may independently change the selection; a zoom gesture does not guarantee a fixed dataset when other events occur. Preserve the focused identity where possible and convey incomplete coverage.

Support a compact bird's-eye work view; approximately eight cells per row and 100 simultaneously visible objects illustrate the intended scale, not fixed columns, a device-independent fit guarantee or a performance benchmark.
Distinguish PR and Issue at compact scale and expose meaningful state without relying on color alone. More information can appear as cells grow; content adapts to available space and text size.

A boundary transition enters the intended object or scope at the next level; do not infer a different target when it is ambiguous. Return retains valid scope, applicable filters and scale and restores position when possible. How the target is established and exact reverse-transition behavior remain open.

First-version long-press preview supports inspecting an object before opening it. A later sliding rich preview lets the operator inspect neighboring cells without leaving the dense overview; its activation and gesture arbitration remain open.

Offer an accessible way to change density and open or inspect an object without requiring pinch, precise tiny targets or color alone. Adapt layout for large text rather than forcing the illustrative column count.

Prefer iOS system appearance, colors, typography and SF Symbols with restrained Liquid Glass in keeping with the selected Apple Look; exact components remain subject to design and platform validation.

The owner envisages a further pinch out from Today to a farthest calendar of daily work intensity in the applicable Project scope under 0018. This proposed outward transition is distinct from the selected expanding-cell maximum; precise threshold, gesture details and first-version scope remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Pinch changes detail in discrete steps; on reaching maximum cell size it transitions to the intended next level when the target is unambiguous, with the threshold depending on grid width and maximum cell size in points.
Dense view supports the intended scale of approximately 100 simultaneously visible objects without treating illustrative object and column counts as fixed device-independent requirements.
Object type and meaningful state remain accessible without reliance on color or pinch alone.
A boundary transition retains the intended target and valid context; returning preserves valid context where possible.

nodes.title: GitView - Preview and future sliding inspection
nodes.description: Let the operator inspect an object without losing the surrounding bird's-eye overview.

requirements.statement: A recognized long press on an eligible Project, Repository, PR or Issue opens a static preview of that same object, exposing additional available permitted details readably without leaving the overview. The operator can explicitly open that object or dismiss the preview without navigating.

The preview and any explicit opening retain the selected object's identity and permitted source context; an object with the same visible name or number is not substituted. Apply the current access policy.

Dismissing the preview or returning from an object preserves valid originating scope, period, filters and density, restoring position when possible. When the origin is no longer valid or cannot be verified, provide an available meaningful fallback without silently claiming the old scope.
Offer accessible alternatives to long press for preview, dismissal and direct object opening. Direct opening does not replace access to preview.

A later rich preview can update a single bubble as the operator moves across cells, inspecting objects without navigating into each and without leaving the dense overview. Its content corresponds to the current object under the finger; a delayed result for a prior object is not presented as the current object's details. This is not a first-version prerequisite. Long press as its activation remains a hypothesis; pointer hover is optional and is not available on every device.
Unknown or stale displayed details keep their limitations; a preview must not establish success or identity from missing data or bypass applicable restrictions.

For a private Repository whose access revocation is explicitly established under 0019, continue to show already saved local details in the applicable preview, including one open when the revocation is established, with an access-revoked indication and supported last update time when known. Stop synchronization of the affected Repository; retained local visibility is not GitHub access, and a missing time is not invented. Independently applicable disclosure restrictions still apply; freshness is attributed to the supported observations. Other access and account cases remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: First-version preview presents readable additional available permitted details for the same eligible object on recognized long press without leaving the overview, and offers explicit open and dismissal.
Accessible non-long-press paths support preview, dismissal and direct opening.
Valid origin context is retained on dismissal or return; an invalid origin is not silently substituted.
Sliding rich inspection remains a later direction with activation and gesture details open.

An already open preview of saved permitted private data remains visible on confirmed revocation with its indication and supported update time when known, without implying source access. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Original source and sharing
nodes.description: Let the operator reach the original GitHub object and share useful context from the overview.

requirements.statement: For a Repository, PR or Issue with an eligible source-associated GitHub URL, offer a route to that source object. Associate the URL with the correct object and source context. If no eligible URL is known, indicate unavailability rather than inventing a confirmed URL or substituting another object.

Offer lightweight sharing using the platform's native sharing experience when applicable, subject to the selected access and handoff policy. The exact content and default payload require separate refinement.

Sharing a link does not grant recipient access, establish delivery or prove the external handler loaded the intended object. Do not claim any of these outcomes merely because the share flow or source handoff was initiated.

Current applicable access and disclosure restrictions govern source handoff and shared material. A previously observed address is not automatically eligible if its identity, direction or current disclosure is uncertain.
Source-link-only sharing without automatic private text, repository contents or screenshots is an agent-authored candidate, not an independently selected owner requirement.
Sharing the local Project itself is not required for now. This does not remove lightweight sharing of eligible GitHub Repository, PR or Issue context.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An eligible known GitHub source link remains associated with its correct object and Repository context.
Offer a source-opening route for an eligible known URL and native lightweight sharing when applicable.
If source-link sharing is offered but no eligible link is available, show that link sharing is unavailable; other separately authorized payloads remain open.
Lightweight sharing does not itself grant recipient access or establish delivery.
Missing or ineligible source evidence is not replaced by a fabricated or misdirected URL.

nodes.title: GitView - Accessibility and platform behavior
nodes.description: Make overview, preview and object access usable with platform accessibility features.

requirements.statement: Essential navigation, density, preview, dismissal and opening must not rely exclusively on pinch, long press, pointer hover, precise tiny targets or color. Direct object opening does not replace accessible preview.

Assistive technologies receive understandable object type, permitted identity and source context, relevant known state and limitations. Unknown and stale observations retain their status and applicable scope and time when supported; stale success is not announced as current. Unknown data is not announced as success. Confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide already saved local information under 0019; accessible descriptions retain its applicable revocation indication and supported time when known. Other account and external-disclosure cases remain open.
Adapt layout to Dynamic Type and interaction to Reduce Motion. Large text can require fewer columns; motion must not be necessary to understand navigation.
On dismissal or return, restore accessibility focus to the original object when available and valid, or provide a sensible available fallback without silently switching origin.
Prefer system iOS typography, colors, SF Symbols and native controls where appropriate, consistent with the selected Apple Look.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Essential interactions have accessible alternatives to a single gesture and color-only communication.
Assistive descriptions preserve supported identity, known state and applicable uncertainty; confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide saved local content under 0019.
Larger text and Reduce Motion retain understandable content and navigation without fixed density.
Return focus uses the valid original object when available or a sensible available fallback.

nodes.title: GitView - Possible calendar view and later depth
nodes.description: Describe the owner-envisaged farthest calendar view over work intensity and preserve deeper PR exploration as a possible later direction.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Calendar day cells in this envisaged time view are not confused with Project, Repository or work-object identity cells.
An unavailable historical value is not described as a confirmed zero.
Contribution activity is not equated with completed work, successful CI or approved review.
Calendar and deeper PR browsing are not prerequisites for the first-version grid and preview; whether the calendar itself is included in that version remains open.
The envisaged calendar uses daily work intensity for its applicable selected Project scope; cells do not show individual CI or health indicators, and the exact intensity definition remains open.
The owner-envisaged route reaches the calendar by further pinch-out from Today; exact interaction and inclusion in the first version remain open.

nodes.title: GitView - GitHub access and repository discovery
nodes.description: Provide the operator a path to connect GitHub and find eligible repositories for a GitView Project.

requirements.statement: Offer a way for the operator to authorize access and identify the connected GitHub source account. GitView User is the operator and need not be the author or assignee of any source object.

Support finding and selecting Repositories available to the connected account for Project composition. Incomplete discovery or insufficient access is distinguishable from a confirmed empty result; a selection alone does not establish a saved Project or an independent source grant.

Protect credentials using platform-provided secure storage and do not include them in shared content or ordinary diagnostics. Exact authorization and permission requirements require source-specific refinement.

Distinguish an explicit authentication or permission denial from a temporary network failure and a successful empty result. Failure alone does not erase accepted observations or prove deletion; the owner's specific explicit-revocation behavior below applies only when supported for the affected Repository.

When GitHub explicitly confirms that access to a private Repository is revoked for the relevant account, keep the already saved local data. While that account remains active, continue showing it as last known with an explicit access-revoked indication and supported last update time when known; the account_change boundary applies when another account is active. Stop synchronization of that Repository while the revocation applies; a late response must not silently restart synchronization or present itself as a new accepted update after revocation. Do not fabricate an update time, treat temporary network failure or a 404 alone as proof of revocation, or claim that retained local visibility restores GitHub access. Exact evidence, presentation, recovery and other account-change behavior require refinement.

While the relevant account remains active after revocation, preserve a discoverable local entry point for understanding it, pursuing access recovery and explicitly deleting locally retained data. The available local view and user control do not establish a restored GitHub grant, guarantee successful recovery, or delete source objects. Exact native controls and recovery mechanics remain open.

Provide an intentional way to disconnect or reconnect. When GitHub account B is active, do not show private data previously saved from account A. This visibility rule does not itself delete A’s stored data or determine behavior after returning to A. An external GitHub access revocation is distinct from switching accounts: while the relevant account remains active, saved private data remains visible under revoked_private with its indication and supported time when known. Other disconnect, account and credential-removal cases remain open.

GitView is an overview with a path to GitHub; source authorization or installation is distinct from modifying a PR, Issue or Repository. Additional write features and account models are outside this node's selected scope.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The operator can initiate and complete supported source authorization and identify the connected account.
The operator can select an eligible discovered Repository for Project composition without treating selection alone as a saved Project.
Discovery distinguishes an incomplete or access-limited result from a confirmed empty result.
Credentials are protected and are not included in shared content or ordinary diagnostics.
A network error is not represented as a confirmed source denial, deletion or successful empty result.
Local disconnection does not by itself delete GitHub Repositories.

Explicitly revoked private Repository data remains local; while its account remains active it is visible with a revocation indication and supported update time when known. Synchronization stops while revocation applies; the selected account-change boundary applies when B is active.
After confirmed revocation while its account remains active, the saved Repository remains a discoverable entry point for understanding the limitation, access recovery and explicit local deletion.
While account B is active, previously saved private data from account A is not shown; switching accounts does not itself delete that data.

nodes.title: GitView - Product journey and acceptance direction
nodes.description: Describe a coherent product journey and observable outcomes without declaring the specification graph or implementation complete.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The described supported path connects Project setup, overview, work selection, inspection and an eligible GitHub source route.
Unfinished and same-day completed work, persistent filters and the bounded historical merged-counter override retain their distinct meanings.
Refresh failures, restricted or incomplete data and unavailable history are not presented as confirmed healthy, complete or empty results.
Product requirements remain distinct from proof of implementation, integration, device behavior or release readiness.

nodes.title: GitView - Testability and architecture direction
nodes.description: Make product behavior testable and guide implementation without choosing a premature module structure.

requirements.statement: Use FSD iOS as the intended direction for organizing app responsibilities. Define actual layers and dependencies when responsibilities are understood; do not require empty modules or assume unverified source versions.

Use SpecificationCore for suitable named domain decisions where it clarifies composition and testability. Preserve meaningful results such as unknown when required; selection of exact policies and integration remains open.

Make network, data persistence and other nondeterministic dependencies replaceable at appropriate boundaries. A particular DI framework or a protocol for every type is not required by this product direction.

Develop product behavior with TDD and provide appropriate deterministic network and data mocks, stubs or fakes; exercise meaningful success, failure and uncertainty. Choose each test double for the scenario rather than mandating a specific implementation for every test.
Independently tested domain decisions do not prove a live GitHub integration or native UI works. Verify relevant adapters and integration paths separately when implementation exists.
Preserve source, scope, freshness and uncertainty across decisions and presentation instead of coercing unknown observations into success or zero.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The architecture direction includes FSD iOS and appropriately selected SpecificationCore decisions without claiming integration exists.
Network and data dependencies are replaceable for meaningful deterministic TDD with suitable test doubles.
Unknown and partial source information retain their meanings across decisions and presentation.
Passing isolated tests is not presented as proof of live GitHub or native UI integration.

nodes.title: GitView - First launch and Project setup
nodes.description: Let the operator progress from an empty Project collection to a GitHub-backed Project without confusing missing data and failures.

requirements.statement: When a supported current local read establishes an empty Project collection, offer a discoverable path toward GitHub connection and repository selection. An unreadable or incomplete local collection is not a confirmed empty collection or evidence that the app has never been used. Preserve existing saved Projects and membership; make the local limitation and a supported retry discoverable without promising recovery.

The operator can initiate authorization and discover eligible repositories under 0019. Cancellation or failure leaves an understandable path to continue and does not establish a connected account or successful empty source. Cancellation or failure alone does not delete saved Projects or accepted observations; display remains subject to the applicable access policy.

A partially observed repository collection remains incomplete, not an exhaustive list. Make the limitation visible, offer supported permitted results for selection and a supported retry where available. A confirmed zero matches only its actual search and access scope; no search match does not prove an empty account. Choosing a Repository does not by itself prove that a Project was saved or that all work was observed.

Support one default Project per eligible Repository while keeping Project and Repository distinct. A Project may contain more Repositories or share one with another Project under 0005; the exact setup mechanism is open. If a multi-Repository default selection is supported, its default corresponds to one Project per Repository, not an implicitly combined Project; this does not mandate multi-selection or a specific association.

Distinguish a supported successful Project save from failure or indeterminate result. Do not silently create a duplicate while an earlier possible creation effect remains unresolved; recovery depends on available evidence and is not guaranteed.

Once a valid Project is established, distinguish work still unobserved or loading from a confirmed empty list. A successfully saved, identifiable and permitted Project can be reached and opened into its work. An authorized account or selected Repository is not itself evidence that PR and Issue data has been obtained.

acceptance_criteria.statement: With an eligible selected Repository and successful required operations, the operator can complete default setup and open the saved identifiable Project's permitted work.
A supported empty collection offers a path to connect and select Repositories without equating incomplete data with emptiness.
Cancellation, failure and indeterminate save do not fabricate successful authorization or a saved Project.
The selected default retains Project and Repository as distinct and does not imply work data is already loaded.
A successfully saved, identifiable and permitted Project can be opened into its work; unobserved work remains distinct from empty.
Existing accepted configuration is not erased by cancellation or failure; partial and uncertain outcomes remain distinguishable.

nodes.title: GitView - Project overview observation states
nodes.description: Help the operator understand what the Project overview knows, what remains unknown and when previously observed information was updated.

requirements.statement: Distinguish a confirmed absence of locally configured Projects from an unreadable or not-yet-observed configuration. Neither alone establishes that GitHub has no repositories or work. Preserve saved configuration when its read fails and provide an appropriate recovery route.

Distinguish unobserved, incomplete, failed and last-known observations from confirmed empty results and supported zero values. Values retain their actual scope, supported observation time and coverage; do not promote one successful category to a complete Project observation.

When a source refresh fails, continue presenting available saved data with its supported observation time when known and a discoverable scoped failure or limitation. Do not claim successful refresh, a source denial or an empty collection solely because of a network failure.

If GitHub explicitly confirms access revocation for a private Repository, previously saved local information remains visible with the revocation indication and supported last update time when known under 0019. Synchronization of that Repository stops while revocation applies. Keep a discoverable entry point to understand the limitation, pursue access recovery and explicitly delete local data; do not imply a restored GitHub grant.

Make meaningful values and loading, coverage, failure and access distinctions available to assistive technologies and without relying on color alone, including accessible paths to the applicable recovery or local action.
A 404 or temporary network failure alone does not establish revocation or deletion. Other account and disclosure cases retain their separate open questions under 0019 and 0024.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A confirmed empty local Project collection is distinguishable from unreadable configuration, unobserved work and incomplete or failed source observation.
Available saved observations remain visible with their supported scope and time when known, and a refresh failure does not silently turn them into a confirmed empty result or a fresh observation.

Confirmed private Repository revocation keeps saved local data visible with its indication and supported update time when known, stops synchronization and preserves accessible recovery and explicit local deletion entry points under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Meaningful observation and access distinctions and the applicable actions are available without relying on color alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Navigation context and restoration
nodes.description: Preserve understandable navigation context while moving among Projects, work collections and object overviews.

requirements.statement: Applicable navigation context includes Project identity, Repository scope, period, filters, density and position or focused object when available. These are presentation state, not new domain entities.

Returning from a PR or Issue retains valid originating Project, scope, applicable period, filters and density and restores a permitted position or focused object by identity where possible. A saved index or matching display name alone does not establish the same object.

If the original object, Repository or Project is unavailable, removed, restricted or unverifiable, do not silently substitute another object or scope as the original. Distinguish a confirmed change from an unobserved or incomplete result; provide an available access-safe fallback or recovery path appropriate to the supported facts.

Changing density within a scope does not itself change the selected Project, Repository scope, period or filters. Independent updates may change the supported collection and retain their own observation context. At the maximum cell-size boundary an intentional pinch transition to the next level follows 0014 while retaining the intended target and applicable context.

Explicitly selected lifecycle filters persist and restore when applicable under 0007. The selected historical merged counter exception under 0047 is a temporary transition override and does not itself rewrite the saved preference. Other signal-origin transitions retain the actual applicable source filter context under 0092 without rewriting saved preferences; unrelated filters do not narrow a signal produced outside their scope.

Revalidate current applicability and independently applicable disclosure restrictions before showing retained content; a saved navigation context is not a GitHub access grant. For confirmed revocation of a private Repository, saved data remains visible under 0019 with revocation and last-update context when known; source access is not required for that local display. Other private-data policies remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Returning from an object retains its valid permitted originating scope, applicable period, filter and density when available.
Missing or inaccessible context is not silently replaced with a different object or treated as a confirmed empty collection.
Before the maximum-size boundary, pinch density changes preserve scope, period and filters; an intentional boundary transition follows 0014, and independent source changes remain distinguishable.
Saved filters and the limited historical merged-counter override follow 0007 and 0047 without silently rewriting preferences.

nodes.title: GitView - Project lifecycle and membership
nodes.description: Let the operator create and manage local Projects without confusing their identities or changing the source Repositories.

requirements.statement: A saved Project has a stable local identity, name, optional description and one or more source-identified GitHub Repositories. Project identity is distinct from its name, a Repository address and GitHub organization metadata.

A Repository can belong to several Projects, and a Project can contain Repositories from different GitHub organizations. A membership change in one Project does not itself alter another Project or mutate the GitHub Repository.

By default there is one Project per Repository under 0005. How an existing default is identified, reused or recovered remains open; do not assume an arbitrary Project containing that Repository is its default.

The operator can create, rename and edit a Project and select its members. A valid saved Project contains at least one Repository; an invalid attempt to remove the final member does not become a confirmed empty Project. Exact controls, name validation and intermediate editing behavior remain open.

The optional local Project description can be inspected and explicitly changed or cleared without changing the Project identity or the GitHub Repository description. An unavailable description is not automatically a confirmed absent one.

An intentional local Project removal affects the selected local Project. It does not imply deletion of the GitHub Repository or remove another Project's membership. Details of confirmation, retained observations and recovery require refinement.

When GitHub confirms the same Repository after rename or transfer, preserve the Repository identity, prior history and its Project memberships under 0002. A name or address alone is not identity evidence.

An unavailable configuration read or indeterminate save does not prove a Project or membership absent, a save successful or a duplicate safe. Preserve and reconcile supported local information where possible, and make unresolved outcomes discoverable without inventing an old or new complete state. If a saved configuration is inconsistent and its validity cannot be established, do not present its membership as confirmed.

Confirmed GitHub revocation alone does not hide an already saved local Project or its saved Repository information under 0019; show the applicable indication and supported time when known. Local visibility does not grant source access or authorize a new Project admission. Revocation alone does not remove saved Project membership.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A saved Project has a stable local identity, name and at least one Repository, and is distinct from its members and GitHub organizations.
A Repository may belong to multiple Projects; a valid edit to one does not change another Project or the GitHub Repository.
The default of one Project per Repository does not by itself select a persistent default-association mechanism.
Rename or transfer with confirmed same Repository identity preserves history and Project memberships.
Unavailable configuration or an indeterminate save is not treated as confirmed absence, success or a safe duplicate.
Confirmed GitHub revocation alone does not hide already saved local Project information under 0019.
The optional local Project description can be explicitly changed or cleared without changing Project identity or the GitHub Repository description.
Intentional local Project removal does not delete the GitHub Repository or alter membership in other Projects.

nodes.title: GitView - Scoped observations and incomplete refresh
nodes.description: Preserve the meaning and scope of observed information when GitHub refresh succeeds, partially succeeds or fails.

requirements.statement: Associate each supported observation with its actual Repository or Project scope, category and observation time where known. A successful observation in one scope or category does not make another current or complete.

Present a collection as fully observed or a supported zero only when the available evidence establishes that result for its actual scope. A successful request or one successful category alone does not prove complete Project or account coverage.

When only part of the requested information is supported, preserve independently known results and make incomplete coverage discoverable. A partial response does not turn missing items into zero, silently erase earlier observations or claim a complete refreshed collection.

After a failed refresh, retain available previously saved data with its supported observation time when known and a discoverable scoped failure. Do not invent an unknown time. A failed attempt does not advance the last successful observation time or establish source deletion, denial or emptiness by itself.
Request a refresh of displayed information from GitHub when applicable; do not present older saved information as a successful new update when the latest refresh could not establish it.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository retains the saved local data and shows its revocation indication and supported time when known under 0019. Stop synchronization for the affected Repository while revocation applies; a late in-flight response is not presented as a fresh accepted update merely because it arrives afterward.
The operator can discover a refresh failure or incomplete coverage and understand the available time and scope without relying solely on color or a transient notice.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Observation scope, supported time, coverage and latest refresh outcome remain distinguishable.

A failed refresh alone does not advance a successful observation time. A partial refresh does not prove a complete or empty collection, erase earlier saved data or advance the last complete observation time for the wider scope; an independently supported successful part retains its own actual scope and time.
The operator can distinguish a successful update from last-known data after a failed refresh.

Confirmed private Repository revocation preserves available saved local data with its indication and supported time when known, while synchronization stops under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Failure and incomplete coverage are discoverable without relying solely on color or transient feedback.

nodes.title: GitView - Today selection and uncertain observations
nodes.description: Preserve the selected Today and filter behavior when the application has incomplete or uncertain work observations.

requirements.statement: Apply the owner-selected Today meaning under 0007 in the selected Project and user local calendar day; earlier unfinished work remains eligible and work completed today remains eligible. Completion yesterday alone does not qualify an object today; other applicable conditions may do so.

Without an applicable saved exclusion, show eligible PRs and Issues across their lifecycle states, including merged and closed. A PR merged today remains the same object and stays visible in unfiltered Today while eligible; it leaves an explicitly selected unfinished-only view.

Explicit lifecycle filters can hide applicable states and persist between launches when saved. Restore a valid saved selection in the ordinary view; an unavailable or uncertain save is not reported as confirmed. The limited historical merged-counter override follows 0047 and does not rewrite the saved preference.

A source-confirmed PR or Issue is represented once in a selection even when several conditions apply. PR and Issue remain separate objects, and equal local numbers in different Repositories do not establish identical identity. Do not assert confirmed uniqueness when identity evidence is unresolved.

Missing data or an incomplete refresh alone does not establish that an object matches, does not match, is completed or was deleted. A known object with an unresolved selection condition remains distinguishable from a confirmed match or exclusion; do not invent an unobserved object or an exact count from incomplete coverage.

An independently supported inclusion alternative can contribute to a confirmed match even if another inclusion alternative is unknown, provided all applicable required conditions and active filters are supported as satisfied or do not apply. An unknown required filter keeps the selection outcome uncertain; a supported false required filter can exclude the object without making unrelated unknown facts known.

Preserve the actual time, scope and coverage of saved observations under 0026. An unfiltered grid is not evidence that all GitHub work has been observed. On confirmed private Repository revocation, already saved local data remains accessible with the revocation indication and supported time when known under 0019; synchronization stops for that Repository.
The operator can discover applicable filter state, uncertain data and incomplete coverage without relying solely on color or a transient message. Exact controls remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Applicable earlier unfinished work and work completed during the current user local calendar day remain eligible under 0007.
Without an applicable saved exclusion, eligible PRs and Issues appear across lifecycle states; explicit lifecycle filters persist when saved and do not change source objects.
An incomplete observation does not by itself establish a confirmed match, non-match, deletion or empty source, and supported independent evidence retains its own meaning.
Each included confirmed object has one cell per selection even if multiple conditions apply; linked PR and Issue and same-number objects in different Repositories are not conflated.
Confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide saved local work under 0019 or turn it into newly current source data.

nodes.title: GitView - PR check counters and independent review signals
nodes.description: Let the operator interpret check counts, review assessment and review-thread counts for a PR without mistaking one signal for another.

requirements.statement: Show supported current individual check counts as red, yellow, green and total for the applicable PR, preserving observed revision when known, time and coverage. A workflow run or historical attempt is not automatically another current check; identify current equivalence only where supported by source evidence.

Distinguish a supported zero checks from an unobserved or incomplete collection. Partial observations may support partial counts with visible limitations; an unknown, pending, special or unmapped result is not silently treated as success. The three colored counts are not assumed to sum to total until the applicable mapping supports it.

Keep each check result and review observation associated with its supported revision and observation time when known. An earlier result is not silently presented as current for a newer revision without evidence; unavailable revision or time remains uncertain and is not invented.

Keep the supported source review assessment, review requests, total review threads and unresolved review-thread count independently interpretable. Where supported, distinguish unavailable assessment, absence of reviews and a source-reported review requirement. A request for changes may coexist with zero unresolved threads; zero unresolved threads alone is not approval or merge readiness.

A confirmed current failed check or unresolved thread can support its corresponding positive signal even if the remaining collection is incomplete. Absence of failures or unresolved threads requires adequate evidence for the applicable scope; no observed item alone is not proof of absence.

Count check entries, affected PRs and affected Repositories as different units under 0012 and 0029. Overlapping checks, review and thread signals do not create additional PR identities or independent tasks.

When GitHub revocation of a private Repository is confirmed, previously saved supported observations remain locally accessible with the revocation indication and supported time when known under 0019. Do not represent them as newly refreshed or current for a newer revision without evidence.
This is a compact overview of counters and signals. It does not require showing individual CI runs or review-thread content inside GitView.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Supported current check counts retain the applicable PR, revision when known, observation time when known and collection coverage.
Known zero checks, unobserved checks and incomplete observations remain distinguishable; unknown or special conclusions do not silently become successful checks.
Review assessment, requests and total and unresolved thread counts remain independently interpretable; one does not imply another.
Check counts, affected PR counts and affected Repository counts are not conflated.
No isolated check, review or thread count is presented as a confirmed merge decision.

nodes.title: GitView - Scope and uniqueness of work summaries
nodes.description: Keep Repository, Project and unique portfolio work summaries interpretable when Repositories and attention signals overlap.

requirements.statement: A Repository summary concerns its own supported source objects for the specified category and period where applicable. Rename or transfer does not create a second Repository when the source confirms the same identity under 0002.
A Project summary uses its applicable member Repositories. A Repository shared by two Projects contributes to each Project in its own scope; one Project's membership is not another's.

When a unique portfolio-wide count is presented, count confirmed Repository and source object identities once across overlapping Projects. A linked PR and Issue remain distinct object types; equal local numbers in different Repositories do not prove the same object.

Distinguish individual failed checks from affected PRs and affected Repositories, and distinguish current work from outcomes over a stated period. A single PR may contribute to several independently supported attention signals without becoming several PRs or independent tasks.

Preserve each summary's supported scope, coverage and observation time when known under 0026. Partial coverage may support an explicitly partial result; it is not a confirmed full total and unavailable inputs are not automatically zero. If membership changes, reassess the new scope without rewriting the provenance of an earlier observation.

Confirmed GitHub revocation alone does not hide an already saved supported local summary under 0019; retain its actual scope, coverage, supported time when known and revocation indication. Do not treat it as a newly refreshed source result.

If a summary signal opens a work selection, preserve the originating Project and applicable Repository, condition and period under 0047. A count of checks, threads or events is not automatically the count of resulting PR or Issue cards. If observations changed or coverage is incomplete, keep that limitation visible rather than forcing equality.

Project historical graphs use the current Project composition for the selected period under 0047 and identify that current-membership basis to the operator with applicable coverage. This does not assert which Repositories belonged to the Project in the past; exact historical counter and event semantics remain subject to their own specifications.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Supported summaries identify their actual Repository, Project or portfolio scope, unit, applicable period and coverage.
Shared Repositories contribute within each applicable Project, while any asserted unique portfolio total counts confirmed Repository and source object identities once.
Distinct units and overlapping attention signals are not silently added as separate work items or substituted for destination card counts.
Incomplete source coverage remains identifiable and is not silently treated as zero or as a complete total.

An available saved summary remains local and visible after confirmed GitHub revocation with its supported time when known and applicable limitation under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Time series, coverage and observed outcomes
nodes.description: Present historical work measurements with enough scope and evidence to distinguish progress from missing information.

requirements.statement: Identify a series by its supported subject, unit, source or observation basis, selected scope, time period and coverage. When values are aggregated into buckets, identify the applicable bucket boundaries. Repository and portfolio identity rules follow 0029.

Project historical graphs are recalculated over the Project's current Repository composition for the selected period under 0047. Identify this basis and applicable coverage to the operator; it is not evidence of which Repositories belonged to the Project at a past time.

A count of open work at a past time requires sufficient observation or reliably reconstructible state for that scope and time. A later snapshot alone does not establish earlier values or all intervening transitions.

Keep PR merge outcomes and Issue closure outcomes distinct from open-work snapshots and from each other. Distinguish supported Issue closure reasons and unknown reason; a closed Issue is not automatically a completed task. Do not attribute a current reason to a past closure event without evidence. A link between a PR and Issue does not establish a single measured object or two independent tasks. When the type of a closed object is unknown, do not count it as an Issue or PR, or dismiss it as irrelevant while claiming an exact type-specific total.

Distinguish a count of events in a period from a count of distinct objects with at least one qualifying event. A repeated observation of the same event must not become another event; a distinct-event count requires sufficient identity and source evidence. Match label, time buckets when used and evidence to the stated unit; do not silently substitute one series for another.
