Attribute an observed outcome to its supported source event time rather than the time GitView fetched it. A current state or a latest available timestamp alone does not prove complete earlier event history.

Show a supported zero only when evidence and coverage support zero for that bucket and scope. An unobserved period remains a gap or unknown; a partially observed scope remains explicitly incomplete rather than a confirmed full total.

A previously saved supported series remains locally accessible after confirmed private Repository revocation under 0019, retaining its actual time, scope, coverage and applicable revocation indication. It is not represented as newly refreshed or complete without supporting evidence.

The operator can understand supported unfinished and completed work without waiting for a formal burn-down formula. A specifically labeled burn-down metric requires a separately specified cohort, measurement unit, starting population and transition rules; do not derive that claim by simply adding PR and Issue counts without the definition and sufficient evidence.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A historical series identifies its supported scope, measurement unit, period and coverage.
A Project historical graph identifies current Project composition as its basis and does not present that basis as historical membership.
Unknown or incomplete coverage is not presented as a confirmed zero or complete total.
Open-work snapshots, PR merge outcomes, Issue closure outcomes and event-versus-distinct-object counts are not silently conflated.

Previously saved supported history remains locally accessible after confirmed private Repository revocation under 0019 with its applicable limitation and supported time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Static preview and object identity
nodes.description: Let the operator inspect a selected object without losing its identity or the originating overview.

requirements.statement: A recognized long press previews the selected eligible Project, Repository, PR or Issue without leaving the overview. It provides readable additional available details beyond the cell and offers explicit local open or dismissal. Details retain their supported source context and limitations; unavailable values are not invented.

The preview and an explicit local open remain bound to the selected object's supported identity and originating context. A reordered cell or another object with the same number or name is not substituted. Refresh or filter changes do not silently retarget an already open preview.

Dismissal or return preserves the valid origin, Project, applicable period, filters and density under 0024, with meaningful position or focus where possible. If the origin cannot be restored, expose an appropriate supported fallback rather than implying a different scope is the original.

When GitHub explicitly confirms access revocation for a private Repository, already saved local preview details remain available with the revocation indication and supported last update time when known under 0019. A local open of the same saved object does not establish restored GitHub access. Synchronization stops and applicable recovery or explicit local deletion remains reachable.

Preview, dismissal, explicit opening and return have accessible paths without requiring long press or color alone, with object identity and observation limitations available to assistive technologies under 0032.
Sliding inspection across cells remains a later product direction; its activation and gesture arbitration are not required by this node.

acceptance_criteria.statement: First-version preview provides readable additional available details for the selected object without navigating away and offers explicit local open and dismissal; opening preserves its identity and origin.
Grid reordering, refresh or filter change does not silently retarget an open preview or substitute an unrelated object.
Dismissal and return retain valid origin and selection context or provide a supported fallback without presenting a different object as the original.

Available saved preview details remain locally accessible after confirmed private Repository revocation with the applicable indication and supported time when known under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Preview, dismissal, opening and return have accessible paths that do not require long press or color alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Accessible grid and navigation
nodes.description: Keep the scalable overview, inspection and navigation understandable and operable without relying on sight, color or a particular gesture.

requirements.statement: An accessible representation identifies an object's type and enough supported identity and source context to distinguish it in the current scope. It communicates available relevant status without converting unknown or stale information into a current success.

Provide accessible paths to connect or recover access, select Repositories, manage and navigate Projects, inspect and open work, change grid density, reach filters and available refresh, source or sharing actions, and dismiss or return from preview. These paths do not depend solely on pinch, long press, hover, a particular visual position or color.

When preview is dismissed or an object is closed, restore meaningful focus to the same available object or an appropriate valid context. Do not identify a different object as the original when the selection changed; exact fallback mechanics remain open under 0024.

Make meaningful values, loading, incomplete coverage, failure and source-access state available to assistive technologies and without reliance on color alone. Preserve each supported observation time and scope; do not claim a category refreshed simply because another did.

After confirmed GitHub access revocation for a private Repository, already saved local content remains accessible with the revocation indication and supported last update time when known under 0019. Applicable recovery or explicit local deletion remains accessible; retained local visibility does not imply a GitHub grant.

Larger text, display preferences and reduced motion retain access to essential content and navigation. Exact density and visual transition may adapt; example grid column counts are not accessibility requirements.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Essential overview navigation, density changes, inspection, preview and available refresh or recovery actions have accessible paths without requiring a particular gesture or color.
Accessible representations distinguish object identity and source context and do not present unknown or stale values as confirmed current success.
Dismissal and return preserve meaningful context without silently identifying a different object as the original.

Saved local content remains accessible with the applicable indication and known observation time after confirmed private Repository revocation under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Larger text and reduced motion preserve access to essential information and navigation without a fixed grid density.

nodes.title: GitView - Open and share the original source
nodes.description: Let the operator reach a selected object's original GitHub source and share useful context without confusing the object or implying external access.

requirements.statement: Associate an offered source link with the selected Repository, PR or Issue and its supported source context. Equal local object numbers in different Repositories do not establish identical objects; do not substitute a link belonging to another object.

A previously observed address may remain available as last known where applicable and no contradicting identity evidence exists, with its actual observation context and uncertainty. An old association alone does not establish that the address still resolves to the same object. If source evidence confirms that the address now identifies another object, do not offer it for source opening or sharing as the earlier object; rename, transfer and address reuse are evaluated under 0002 and 0038.

If no eligible association for a source action is supported, provide an understandable unavailable or uncertain state rather than inventing a URL from a name or number or silently navigating to another object.

When an eligible source link is known, offer an action to request opening the source through the platform. Starting or accepting a handoff does not by itself prove the external application loaded the intended object or that GitHub granted access.

Offer lightweight platform sharing when applicable, subject to the separately selected content and disclosure policy. A link-only default is an agent-authored candidate rather than a selected owner requirement; do not assume private text, screenshots or another payload are included or excluded without the applicable decision.

Sharing does not grant a recipient GitHub access, prove delivery or prove that the recipient opened the object. Credentials must not be included in shared material or ordinary diagnostics, including credentials already embedded in an observed URL. Information already handed outside GitView cannot be assumed retractable.

Apply the currently supported object identity, link eligibility and independently applicable disclosure evidence when GitView actually hands the source link or payload to the platform, including a later app-controlled provision if used. Do not claim an earlier render alone proves current eligibility; a previously completed external handoff cannot be assumed retractable.

Confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide an already saved local object or its supported last-known information under 0019. Local visibility does not by itself establish that an external source action or share is eligible; that handoff follows its own policy and must not be reported as successful without evidence.
A failed or cancelled source action does not itself establish source deletion. Preserve an available way back to valid GitView context under 0024.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An offered source link remains associated with the correct selected object and Repository context.
A source-opening action and lightweight platform sharing are available when their applicable eligibility is supported, without asserting external success or delivery.
Missing or conflicting link evidence is not replaced by a fabricated or misdirected source URL.

Local visibility after confirmed private Repository revocation remains distinct from eligibility and outcome of an external handoff. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

Sharing does not itself grant a recipient GitHub access or establish delivery. Credentials, including those already embedded in an observed URL, are not included in shared material or ordinary diagnostics.

nodes.title: GitView - Authored description sections and source text
nodes.description: Preserve what an Issue or PR author wrote while making reliably identified sections understandable as authored statements.

requirements.statement: The selected Issue format contains Problem, Motivation, Expected outcome and References. The selected PR format contains those sections plus Changes and Validation under 0010.
Keep the available original source description accessible with its source context, including unstructured or external text. A confirmed empty body is distinct from an unavailable or unobserved body.

Present a section as extracted only when its authored text can be reliably identified in the source. Preserve the original wording and attribution when available; do not infer missing content from a title, link, review or label.

Missing, empty, duplicated or unsupported headings are not automatically equivalent. When evidence is sufficient to establish a selected section is missing, indicate that absence. If extraction is ambiguous, do not assert confirmed absence; retain the available original body and communicate its limitation rather than inventing sections or hiding the object. Exact extraction and ambiguity rules remain open.

Motivation, expected outcome and validation are statements in an authored description. They do not independently establish an actor's actual motive, achievement of an outcome, successful CI or independent test evidence. Present independently observed source facts according to their own evidence.

A refreshed or newly observed body and an extracted section retain their actual observation context. A section from an earlier body is not presented as though reliably extracted from a later body when source or extraction evidence is unavailable.

After confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository, previously saved local description text remains accessible with the revocation indication and supported observation time when known under 0019; do not imply the source is currently reachable.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Available original Issue and PR descriptions remain accessible even when structured extraction is absent or unreliable.
Reliably extracted sections retain their authored text and are distinguished from independently observed state and evidence.
Empty, unavailable, missing and ambiguous content are not silently conflated or fabricated.
A differently formatted legacy or external description is not sufficient reason to hide its PR or Issue.

Previously saved local text remains accessible after confirmed private Repository revocation under 0019 with its applicable indication and supported time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Density changes within an overview
nodes.description: Let the operator move between a dense overview and more detailed cards without losing the meaning or scope of the selected work.

requirements.statement: Pinch changes grid detail through discrete density steps, with visual feedback as the operator moves between them. At maximum cell size, the gesture transitions to the intended next level under 0014; the boundary depends on grid width and the maximum cell size in points. Approximate examples of eight columns and a hundred objects illustrate desired scale, not fixed counts or a performance guarantee.

Changing density alone does not change the selected Project or Repository, period, explicit filters, object identity, lifecycle state, source observation or collection coverage. An independent refresh or membership change may still alter the collection and retains its own explanation.

Smaller cells can display less detail while preserving an accessible way to distinguish PR from Issue, identify and inspect objects without relying on color alone. Larger cells can reveal more supported information. A detail omitted for lack of space is not an assertion that it is zero, current, complete or healthy.

At the Projects overview, changing density does not change a Project or its actual summary scope. Preserve an available route to the applicable Project summary even when not all values fit in a compact cell.

Preserve the identity of an available focused or anchored object and a meaningful position where possible as density changes. If an independent data or scope change makes it unavailable, use a supported fallback under 0024 without presenting another object as the original.

Before the maximum cell-size boundary, density changes keep the current scope. At the boundary an intentional transition enters the corresponding next level under 0014; ambiguous target selection must not silently open another object. Exact anchoring and reverse behavior remain open.

Provide an accessible alternative to pinch and a way to identify and inspect objects without relying on color or tiny targets alone under 0032. Large text or screen size can change the layout rather than forcing an illustrative column count.
The first-version static preview remains available for an eligible object under 0031. Sliding inspection is a later direction and its activation is not selected here.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Before the boundary, changing density preserves the applicable collection scope, period, filters and object identities; at the boundary the intended next-level transition follows 0014.
Dense and spacious presentations retain accessible identification and inspection of available objects without relying solely on color or pinch.
A focused object remains the same object where it is available; an unavailable origin is not silently replaced by another object.
Larger text can alter the number of columns without removing access to essential content and actions.
Independently observed data changes remain distinguishable from the effect of changing density.

nodes.title: GitView - Connection state and stored observations
nodes.description: Help the operator understand connection problems while retaining access to information already saved locally.

requirements.statement: Distinguish a temporary network failure, a connection or credential problem, an explicitly confirmed Repository access revocation and an intentional disconnect when supported by evidence. A 404 or generic network failure alone does not prove deletion or revocation, and an uncertain cause is not presented as confirmed.

Keep available previously saved local observations accessible where their applicable disclosure is supported, with their supported scope and observation time when known, and make the relevant connection limitation discoverable. For confirmed private Repository revocation the owner-selected visibility rule below applies. Locally readable data is not itself evidence of a current GitHub grant or a successful new refresh.

On confirmed GitHub access revocation for a private Repository, retain its saved local data; while its account remains active show it with the revocation indication and supported last update time when known under 0019. While B is active, the A-to-B visibility boundary applies; stop synchronization for that Repository while revocation applies. Do not accept an earlier in-flight response as a fresh successful update merely because it arrives later.

Retain a discoverable route to understand the connection problem, pursue recovery and intentionally delete local data under 0019, subject to its account-change visibility boundary. Recovery does not guarantee the source grants access, and local deletion does not assert deletion of GitHub objects.

An intentional local disconnect stops new refresh for the affected connection and does not by itself delete saved local information. Handling and disclosure of retained private data after disconnect remain separately open under 0019. Indicate an unresolved credential-removal outcome when known; do not equate a local disconnect with source deletion or provider-side revocation.

Keep observation and operation context attributable to the account and Repository that produced it. While account B is active, previously saved private data from account A is not shown under 0019; switching accounts does not itself delete A’s data. For external GitHub revocation of A’s access while A remains active, saved data remains visible with the selected indication under 0019. Other account isolation and disclosure details remain open.
Make the applicable connection limitation and available recovery or local action discoverable without relying only on color or a transient notice.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A temporary failure is not presented as a confirmed Repository deletion, revocation, empty result or successful refresh without supporting evidence.

Available previously saved observations remain accessible where their applicable disclosure is supported, with time when known and a discoverable connection limitation; confirmed private Repository revocation follows the selected visibility rule. Local visibility does not establish live GitHub access.

Confirmed private Repository revocation preserves saved local data and stops synchronization; while its account remains active, show its indication and supported time when known and retain access both to recovery and to explicit local deletion under 0019.
An intentional disconnect stops new refresh without silently deleting saved local information or claiming that GitHub objects were deleted.
Connection problems and applicable recovery paths are available without relying solely on color or transient feedback.

nodes.title: GitView - Overview refresh and access changes
nodes.description: Keep the operator oriented when an overview refreshes or access changes while it is open.

requirements.statement: Request an update of the available overview from GitHub while keeping its Project and Repository context. Make the supported update time and any failed or incomplete update discoverable. Preserve available last-known data rather than presenting an unsuccessful update as current.
If only part of a Project refreshes, show available information with its actual scope and indicate the limitation; an unavailable part is not presented as an empty repository.

When GitHub confirms private Repository access revocation, retain saved data visibly with the access-revoked indication and supported last update time when known under 0019; stop synchronization for the affected Repository. Provide both recovery and explicit local deletion entry points under 0019.
Do not present one GitHub account's observations as proof of another account's access. Other disclosure and recovery after account changes beyond the selected A-to-B rule in 0019 remain open.
Do not present an intentionally cancelled update as a successful refresh or automatically label the user's cancellation as a failure.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The overview retains its Project and Repository context and shows supported update information.
Failure or partial refresh does not silently erase saved information or present unavailable work as empty.

Confirmed private Repository revocation keeps saved data visible with its indication and supported time when known, stops synchronization and retains access to both recovery and explicit local deletion under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Observations are not attributed as proof of a different account's GitHub access.

nodes.title: GitView - Repository identity under incomplete observations
nodes.description: Preserve Repository identity, history and Project memberships without guessing when source observations are incomplete.

requirements.statement: Under the owner-approved ontology policy and 0002, compare confirmed numeric REST repository IDs within one GitHub instance: the same ID identifies the same Repository and a different ID a different Repository. The earlier numeric examples and later ontology approval are distinct decision evidence. An ID match does not by itself prove a transfer or current source access.

Repository owner, name and address are observed attributes, not identity by themselves. When sufficiently supported evidence establishes a current changed address for the same Repository, retain its identity, history and all Project memberships.

An observation missing the identity evidence needed to apply the selected rule does not by itself merge records, transfer memberships, establish deletion or prove a new Repository. Preserve the supported prior context and identify the unresolved state rather than guessing from name or address.

If supported source evidence establishes that an old address now identifies a different Repository, do not transfer the earlier Repository's history or Project memberships to the new identity merely because of that address.

A 404, failed request or incomplete discovery alone does not establish deletion or access revocation. Keep supported last-known identity and membership information; confirmed private Repository revocation alone does not hide already saved local information; visibility follows the active-account boundary under 0019.
Retaining existing history does not imply that GitView has a complete source history or can reconstruct information it never observed.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Source-confirmed same Repository identity across rename or transfer preserves existing history and Project memberships.
A changed or reused address alone does not merge identities or transfer an earlier Repository's history and memberships.
Insufficient evidence remains uncertain and does not itself prove deletion or a current address.
A 404 or incomplete discovery alone is not treated as confirmed deletion or revocation.
Confirmed private Repository revocation alone does not hide already saved local information; visibility follows the active-account boundary under 0019.
Same-instance numeric REST repository ID comparison follows the selected ontology policy without inferring an unobserved transfer or current access.

nodes.title: GitView - Issue state, links and discussion counters
nodes.description: Make the selected Issue facts and relationships inspectable without conflating source state, discussion and inferred intent.

requirements.statement: Keep the selected Issue associated with its supported source identity, Repository context and repository-local number. Same-number Issues in different Repositories remain distinct. Present available title, original description and source link without inventing missing values.

Distinguish the source open or closed state, supported closure reason, labels and Issue type. A closed Issue is not automatically completed; an unavailable reason remains unknown. A GitView Project is not a GitHub Projects status.

Present supported author, assignees and milestone as source context. An assignee does not by itself establish that work began; author or assignee does not automatically identify the GitView operator or the actor behind a change.

Preserve supported meanings and direction of linked PRs, mentions, closing references, parent and direct sub-Issues, blocked-by and blocking relationships. A mention is not automatically a closing reference; a relationship alone does not prove completion, an actor's motive or causal history. Incomplete relationship coverage is not a confirmed absence.
If the same source-confirmed PR has both a mention and a closing-reference meaning, identify it once in its Repository context while retaining both supported meanings.

A source-confirmed PR represented in an Issue collection is not presented or counted as an independent Issue even if its correspondence to a separately observed PR remains unresolved. Where source evidence identifies both representations as the same PR, do not double count it. If type or identity correspondence is insufficiently supported, preserve uncertainty rather than guessing from IDs. A genuinely separate Issue linked to a PR remains distinct.

Show supported comment and discussion-participant counts as distinct units and distinguish a known zero from unavailable or partial data. Issue comments are not PR review threads; individual comments and participant lists are not required by this overview. Exact source mapping for the selected participant meaning remains open.

Show supported counts of total and closed direct sub-Issues separately. Do not treat those counts as all transitive descendants or as a percentage of completed work; a closed child may have an unknown or non-completion reason.

Distinguish supported source creation, update, closure and last-comment times from the time GitView observed them, retaining the observation source when supported. A fresh observation of one field does not automatically refresh another.

Make the selected available Issue facts and relationships inspectable in the Issue overview without requiring every field to fit in a grid cell or preview. Where an excerpt is presented, retain access to the available original authored body under 0034; source opening and sharing follow 0033.

After confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository, keep previously saved supported Issue information locally accessible under 0019 with the indication and supported update time when known; do not present it as a newly refreshed result or a source grant.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The selected Issue retains its supported identity and Repository context; state, closure reason, type and labels are not silently conflated.
Supported closing references, mentions, hierarchy and dependency directions remain distinguishable, and links do not prove an actor's motive or completion.
Comment, discussion-participant and direct-sub-Issue counts retain distinct units; unknown or partial values are not presented as zero or completion percentage.
Selected available Issue fields and relationships are inspectable without requiring them all to fit in the cell or preview.

Previously saved supported Issue information remains locally accessible after confirmed private Repository revocation under 0019 with the applicable limitation. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Testable behavior and injected dependencies
nodes.description: Make product behavior independently testable while preserving evidence of real integration.

requirements.statement: Supply network and persistence dependencies at replaceable boundaries; control time, scheduling and other nondeterministic inputs where they affect the scenario. This does not require a DI framework or a protocol for every value.

Exercise suitable named domain decisions with supplied facts, source evidence and time without a live GitHub request or mutation of personal data. Evaluation itself does not read the network or persistence, or perform UI actions. Preserve unknown as distinct from confirmed positive and negative results where the product contract requires it, under 0021.

Use scenario-appropriate network and data fakes, stubs or mocks for reproducible success, partial results, failures and relevant ordering. Verify interactions where they are part of behavior; a single kind of double is not mandatory for every test.

For a behavioral change, first express the intended observable behavior in a failing automated test, implement the minimum to pass, then refactor while retaining passing tests. A behavioral failure is distinct from an unavailable environment or compiler error. Tests should verify meaningful outcomes rather than reproduce every private helper.

Isolated tests establish only behavior under their supplied conditions. Verify real adapter, source, system and native interaction boundaries separately when their contracts need such evidence; do not present an unperformed integration or device check as passed.
Test fixtures and logs exclude credentials and unapproved private source content. Isolated tests do not change the user's actual GitHub state.

Identify the tested specification, scenario, conditions and observed result; distinguish proposed tests from executed tests and behavioral failures from environment failures. A separate draft 0079 proposes further TDD review detail but is not established by this node.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Relevant external effects are replaceable for deterministic behavior tests without live GitHub or personal data mutation.
TDD starts with a behavioral failure, implements the minimum to pass, and refactors with tests passing; an environment failure is not substituted for the initial behavioral failure.
Appropriate doubles exercise supported failure and uncertainty without claiming real integration works.
Verification reports distinguish performed observations from proposed or unperformed checks.

nodes.title: GitView - PR overview facts and change counters
nodes.description: Make the selected PR's compact facts, change counters and independent signals inspectable in the correct source context.

requirements.statement: Retain the selected PR's supported source identity, Repository context and repository-local number. Present available title, original description and source link without replacing missing values or selecting another same-number PR in a different Repository.

Distinguish open, closed without merge and merged from the separately supported draft flag, labels, review assessment and CI. An unavailable lifecycle or signal remains unknown rather than being inferred from another field.

Present supported source and target branches, the PR-associated Repository, separately supported base or target and head or source Repositories, observed revision, author, requested reviewers and related Issues in their actual source contexts. An unavailable base or head Repository is not automatically replaced with the PR-associated Repository. Preserve supported mention and closing-reference meanings independently; a related Issue alone does not prove an actor motive or causal history.

Present supported additions and deletions separately, changed-file count and commit count with their applicable observation context. Unavailable counts are not zero; these counts do not require a diff, file browser or commit-by-commit view inside GitView.

Present current check counters under 0028 and independently supported review assessment, requested-review information and total and unresolved review-thread counts. Incomplete or stale observations retain their limitations; individual run or review-thread content is not required by this overview.

Attribute values to their supported source revision, scope, observation time and observation source when known. Distinguish supported PR creation, update, closure and merge times from the time GitView observed them; unavailable values are not invented. A newly observed title, branch or revision does not automatically refresh omitted review, CI, thread or change-count facts; an earlier value is not silently represented as current for a newer revision.
Preserve available original authored text and reliably supported sections under 0034. An authored validation statement is distinct from independently observed CI and test evidence.

Make the selected available PR facts and their limitations inspectable in the PR overview without requiring all fields to fit simultaneously in a cell or preview. The source route and lightweight sharing follow 0033.

After confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository, previously saved supported PR information remains locally accessible under 0019 with the revocation indication and supported update time when known; it is not thereby newly current or evidence of restored source access.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The selected PR retains its supported identity, PR-associated Repository and separately supported base or head Repository context, including when another Repository contains a same-number PR.
Lifecycle, draft status, review assessment, requested review, check counts, thread counts and change counts remain independently interpretable and unknowns are not presented as zero or approval.
Selected available facts, source event times, observation context and limitations are inspectable without requiring every field to fit in a grid cell or preview; unavailable values are not invented.
Supported additions, deletions, changed-file count and commit count do not require in-app diff, file, commit or run details.

Previously saved supported PR information remains locally accessible after confirmed private Repository revocation under 0019 with its applicable limitation. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Uncertain work selection presentation
nodes.description: Make incomplete work selection understandable while preserving the operator's context and access to already observed work.

requirements.statement: Distinguish a confirmed match from an available identified object whose applicable selection condition remains uncertain, whether its observation is already durably saved or only available from a current partial response. Do not imply persistence without evidence. Unknown source information is not presented as a confirmed match, non-match, deletion, empty collection or successful current result.

Provide a way to inspect an available identified uncertain object and the relevant limitation without inventing an unobserved object or an exact missing count. The treatment preserves actual Project and Repository scope, explicit filters and object identity.

Make incomplete or unobserved collection coverage and the applicable supported observation time when known discoverable even when no individual uncertain object is known. Do not invent an unknown time. A transient message alone is not the only route to that information; exact presentation remains open.
Updates, grouping or ordering changes must not silently substitute another object for one being inspected. Preserve valid focus or an appropriate meaningful fallback under 0024 and 0032.

Confirmed GitHub revocation alone does not hide an already saved local object under 0019. Keep its revocation indication and supported time when known accessible, stop synchronization for the affected Repository and do not claim current source access.
Selection uncertainty, coverage and available inspection or recovery actions are understandable without reliance on color alone or a specific gesture.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A supported confirmed match is distinguishable from an identified object whose applicable selection condition is unknown.
An available uncertain object remains inspectable without inventing unobserved objects, exact missing counts or a confirmed empty collection.
Incomplete coverage and supported observation time when known are discoverable even if no individual missing object is identified; an unknown time is not invented.
Updates and reordering do not silently retarget inspection to a different object.

Saved local private content remains accessible after confirmed GitHub revocation with its indication and supported time when known under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Uncertainty, coverage and applicable actions are understandable without relying solely on color or a specific gesture.

nodes.title: GitView - Understand freshness and incomplete overview
nodes.description: Help the operator understand whether the available Project overview is current and complete enough to use.

requirements.statement: Show available information with its supported update time when known. When an update fails, retain saved data and make the failure discoverable; do not present the failed attempt as a successful update.

When only part of a Project can be updated, keep available results and indicate the relevant limitation. A successful update for one Repository or category does not make all other information current or complete.
Distinguish confirmed empty work or a supported zero from information that has not been obtained or could not be updated. Do not invent an update time or missing objects.

Make the meaning and applicable scope of supported counts and visible work understandable. A count and the number of visible cards can differ because their scope, filters, time or coverage differ; do not invent cards or imply the visible list is complete when it is not known to be. A count alone, even when equal to the number of visible cards, does not establish that every matching object is shown.

After GitHub confirms access revocation for a private Repository, keep saved data visible as last known with the revocation indication and supported update time when known; stop synchronization and retain discoverable routes to both recovery and explicit local deletion under 0019.
Make update status, relevant limitations and available actions understandable without relying on color or transient feedback alone.
When the operator changes Project, day or filters, show results in their actual selected context; an earlier result does not silently replace the newly selected view.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Available saved information remains visible after an unsuccessful refresh with a discoverable failure and supported update time when known.
Incomplete or unavailable information is distinguishable from a confirmed empty result or zero.
Displayed counts and visible cards retain their actual meaning, applicable scope and relevant limitations.

Confirmed private Repository revocation preserves saved data and its indication, stops synchronization and retains both recovery and explicit local deletion under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Status, limitations and available actions are understandable without relying solely on color or transient feedback.

nodes.title: GitView - Repository selection and setup outcomes
nodes.description: Keep Repository selection and the outcome of creating or reusing Project configuration understandable when source or save evidence is incomplete.

requirements.statement: A selection or intended setup is distinct from a successfully saved Project and does not by itself establish source access or observed PR and Issue work. An empty selection does not become a confirmed saved Project with no members.

Interpret a selected entry using supported Repository identity under 0002 and 0038. Equal names or positions alone do not prove two Repositories identical; an unresolved identity remains unresolved instead of silently being matched to another Project.

Support a default of one Project per eligible Repository under 0005 and 0022; this does not limit the later composition of a Project. If a multi-Repository default selection is supported, its default is a separate Project for each Repository rather than one silently combined Project; this does not require multi-selection. How an existing default is recognized, offered or reused when the Repository appears in several Projects remains open; do not silently treat an arbitrary containing Project as the selected default.

Distinguish a supported successful local save from confirmed non-application, pending work and an indeterminate outcome. When multiple setup effects are supported, keep their actual outcomes and Repository identities attributable rather than claiming all succeeded or treating one result as another.

An uncertain save does not prove that no Project was created or that retry is safe. Reconcile against available evidence before repeating a potentially duplicating effect; when the necessary evidence is unavailable, keep the outcome uncertain and offer an applicable recovery path without promising recovery.

Cancellation or failure does not by itself erase previously saved Projects or establish successful source authorization. An unsubmitted selection cancelled by the operator is not subsequently submitted as an effect of that cancelled attempt. Already submitted or independently completed effects retain their supported outcomes and are not claimed undone merely by cancellation.

A partial or failed Repository discovery remains incomplete or failed rather than a confirmed empty source. Keep available supported choices distinguishable from a complete inventory and offer an applicable retry where available.

Confirmed GitHub revocation alone does not hide previously saved local Projects or Repository information under 0019, but local visibility is not a source grant or sufficient evidence to admit a new Project operation.

Provide a way to understand available selection, incomplete discovery and supported save or recovery outcomes without relying solely on color or a transient notification. Exact controls and grouping remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Repository selection is distinguishable from a successfully saved Project and from a loaded work collection.
The default of one Project per Repository remains distinct from the unselected persistent-association mechanism.
Confirmed saved, failed or indeterminate setup effects are not silently conflated; an uncertain effect is not blindly duplicated.
Partial source discovery is not reported as a confirmed empty inventory, and cancellation or failure does not erase already saved Projects.

Saved local Project and Repository information remains accessible after confirmed GitHub revocation under 0019, without implying a source grant for a new operation. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Aggregate counts with incomplete observations
nodes.description: Preserve the meaning and limits of counts derived from observations with differing coverage, time or Project membership.

requirements.statement: Attribute a displayed aggregate to its supported metric, unit, object type, source scope, membership basis, period where applicable, relevant observation times and coverage. Different observation times do not establish an invented simultaneous snapshot.

Evaluate a current Project claim against its actual saved membership. A late result for a previous member set remains attributable to that set; adding an unobserved member can make the new aggregate incomplete, and removal does not imply source deletion. Historical Project graphs use the current Project membership under 0030, not a claim of past membership.

Missing or incomplete input is not zero. A supported partial observation may be shown with its scope and coverage, but does not establish a complete current total. Do not blindly add overlapping observations or assume uniqueness without identity evidence.
A previous observation is not proof of the current population. A stale count of open PRs is not automatically a current lower bound; the earlier value may remain last known with its own context.
A partial later observation does not advance an earlier complete count to a new complete reference or establish an exact later difference without sufficient compatible evidence.

A confirmed positive signal on an identified PR may contribute once to an observed subset with its actual context, even if coverage is incomplete. Absence of a known positive is not proof of a negative when the relevant input is unknown.

When a metric combines separately observed lifecycle, CI or review facts, retain each fact's supported time and revision. Facts observed at different times do not by themselves establish that their combination held simultaneously.

A Repository shared by Projects contributes to each applicable Project; a unique portfolio count deduplicates confirmed identities under 0029. Uncertain identity does not silently become a confirmed unique count.

Confirmed private Repository access revocation preserves saved local observations and supported derived counts as last known, with revocation indication and supported update time when known under 0019; synchronization stops. Do not label the retained data freshly observed, invent a time or replace an unavailable input with zero. Other account-change disclosure beyond the selected A-to-B rule in 0019 remains open.
A present snapshot alone does not prove a historical event count or fill a missing historical bucket; maintain the actual period and coverage under 0030.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Displayed counts retain supported metric, scope, membership basis, time and coverage without inventing a simultaneous snapshot.
Missing or stale observations are not silently treated as zero, an exact current total or a current lower bound.
A late count for prior Project membership is not represented as a complete count for changed membership.

Saved private observations and supported derived counts remain visible after confirmed revocation with an indication and supported update time when known; an unknown time is not invented. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Shared Repository membership is preserved per Project while supported unique portfolio totals deduplicate confirmed identities.

nodes.title: GitView - Project overview and summary
nodes.description: Let the operator survey Projects, understand their work and attention, and enter an applicable selection.

requirements.statement: The overview represents saved GitView Projects whose representation is permitted and identifies them where permitted. A GitHub organization is source metadata, not a GitView Project boundary. A Repository may contribute to each Project containing it.

A Project summary makes available its member Repository count and observation coverage, open PRs with draft as a subset, open Issues, and attention signals for failed CI, waiting for review, changes requested, unresolved thread count and affected PR count, and blocked Issues. It distinguishes merged PR outcomes and Issue closures by reason for a selected period. Show charts of these measurements when sufficient history is available; exact predicates, time ranges and placement remain to be specified. The primary PR «Done» indicator means merged PRs; readiness to merge is a separate desired indicator whose applicable predicate and evidence remain to be defined.

Preserve the meaning and unit of each value. Counts of checks, affected PRs, review threads, Issues and affected Repositories are different measurements; do not add linked PRs and Issues as independent tasks. Affected object and Repository counts may be separately available for the same signal.

Provide the preliminary checks-and-review-passed selection if the corresponding Repository rule is separately defined, accepted and applicable; it is not automatically a guarantee of merge eligibility or an established count before that rule exists.

Parts of the summary presented as comparable use the same applicable period and filters; explicitly distinguish their actual observation contexts and avoid suggesting incompatible values are directly comparable.

A missing or inaccessible observation is not a confirmed zero or healthy result. A Project remains represented when one of its members is unobserved if the representation itself is permitted; otherwise convey an access-safe limitation at a permitted scope when one can be disclosed without revealing restricted existence; non-disclosure alone does not establish an empty or complete scope. Supported partial information retains its limitations, observation context and applicable access restrictions. Do not infer one category's freshness from another category's refresh.

Distinguish current observations from outcomes over a selected period. A graph needs sufficient evidence for its own metric and time scope; unavailable history is not a fabricated zero or a copy of the current value.

Project historical graphs use current Project Repository membership over the selected period as described in 0013. Identify that basis and preserve incomplete history and access limitations; do not present it as the actual Project composition at earlier dates.

An actionable Project signal opens its corresponding selection across the applicable Project member scope as described by 0006, retaining the condition and permitted source context. A selection and its earlier summary need not have equal counts after facts change; preserve their respective observation context and coverage. On an explicit historical merged-PR counter transition, temporarily override a saved exclusion of merged PRs, so the supported result can be shown. This transition does not itself rewrite the saved filter; source coverage, access and the counter's historical period remain applicable. Filter hierarchy and exact return behavior require refinement. A signal originating within a filtered scope retains that scope when opened; a signal originating outside an unrelated filter context is not narrowed by it under 0092. The previously selected historical merged-counter case concerns a counter whose originating scope includes merged PRs; a saved exclusion outside that origin does not narrow its destination. A counter defined inside a merged-excluding scope instead retains that origin scope.

A Repository shared by two Projects contributes to each applicable Project summary. Any combined portfolio total of unique Repositories or source objects counts each supported identity once rather than simply summing Project totals.

The overview uses a zoomable Project grid and makes summary information inspectable without requiring all details to fit a compact cell. Exact density, accessible controls and arrangement remain open.

When GitHub confirms private Repository access revocation, keep the saved Project and available local summary information for the affected Repository visible as last known with the revocation indication and supported update time when known. Stop synchronization for the affected Repository and preserve a discoverable path to recovery or explicit local deletion under 0019. Other account-change disclosure cases remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: For the selected counter whose originating scope includes merged PRs and whose saved merged exclusion is outside that scope: A historical merged-PR counter transition temporarily overrides a saved exclusion of merged PRs without itself rewriting the saved preference; supported period, scope and coverage remain distinct.
A permitted Project summary distinguishes membership and coverage, current work, attention and period outcomes by their meanings.
Draft PRs are a subset of open PRs, and unlike units are not presented as the same count or as independent tasks.
Missing observations and missing historical evidence remain distinguishable from confirmed zeros.
Shared Repository contributions are correct in each Project and any claimed unique portfolio total.
An actionable signal reaches its corresponding scoped selection without assuming unchanged observations or full coverage.

Confirmed private Repository revocation keeps the saved Project and available local summary information for the affected Repository visible with its indication and supported time when known under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Refresh triggers and visible outcomes
nodes.description: Let the operator request or benefit from bounded refresh while understanding what has actually updated.

requirements.statement: Offer pull-to-refresh where appropriate or an equivalent explicit and accessible action for the current view or selected scope. A manual request is not rejected solely because the observation is younger than an eventual staleness threshold; applicable access, source-directed waits and execution constraints still apply. Requesting refresh does not itself establish that it started, completed or succeeded.

Make recoverable saved data available where eligible for local display under 0019 without waiting for a GitHub response. When a relevant scope is opened with stale data, request a bounded update when the applicable access and source constraints permit. Exact staleness, prioritization and scheduling remain open.

The app can request or use a system-granted background opportunity for bounded refresh. iOS controls whether and when the opportunity is granted; no fixed frequency or successful refresh is implied by requesting it.

Preserve the scope and observation context of each actual refresh outcome. A successful Repository metadata or Issue observation does not refresh an unrelated PR scope; a partial response does not establish complete Project coverage.

Make loading, deferred, partial, successful and failed outcomes distinguishable when supported for the affected scope. A request deferred before any source attempt is not described as a completed refresh or a fabricated GitHub failure. For an actual GitHub failure, make the supported error or reason discoverable with the scope and last supported successful time when known; do not invent a source cause or describe a local failure as a GitHub error. Observation and attempt retain their own supported times and scope.

During refresh or failure, previously saved supported data remains available where eligible for local display, with its own observation time when known and applicable limitation under 0003 and 0019. An unobserved collection does not become a confirmed empty result or an invented success time.

Account for shared applicable GitHub rate limits and request cost across manual, foreground and background work; apply supported source retry constraints and avoid unbounded retry loops. An explicit manual request does not bypass an applicable source-directed wait. Exact cost, pagination, concurrency and retry timing remain open.

After confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository, keep its saved local data visible with the revocation indication and supported time when known under 0019; do not dispatch ordinary synchronization for that Repository while revocation applies. Other eligible scopes retain their own context.
The operator can discover applicable refresh state, failure or limitation and available recovery without relying solely on color or transient feedback.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The operator can request refresh using pull-to-refresh where appropriate or an equivalent accessible action.
Saved supported data can remain visible while refresh is requested or in progress; stale-on-open and system-granted background refresh do not imply guaranteed source access or execution frequency.
Partial, deferred and failed outcomes remain distinct from a successful complete observation and are attributed to their actual scopes.
A failed or unattempted request does not invent a successful observation time, confirmed empty source or unsupported GitHub error.
Confirmed private Repository revocation retains previously saved local data under 0019 and prevents ordinary synchronization for that Repository while the revocation applies.

nodes.title: GitView - Today boundary and active navigation
nodes.description: Keep the selected Today view understandable when the user's local calendar day changes while preserving navigation and filter context.

requirements.statement: Interpret the current Today calendar day in the user's local time zone under 0007. Earlier unfinished PRs and Issues remain eligible; work completed during that day remains eligible. Completion on the previous day alone does not establish eligibility for the new Today.

A change in the evaluated Today day or applicable local time-zone context does not by itself change the selected Project, Repository scope, object type or explicit filters. Source event and observation times are not rewritten to fit a new view.

Reevaluate supported selection and coverage for the applicable day, membership and filters. Missing evidence for the new scope remains unknown or incomplete rather than a confirmed empty selection; do not attribute an older day's result to the new day as a fresh observation.

If the applicable Today context changes during an active gesture or while a filter control is open, avoid silently switching the inspected object or clearing the operator's explicit selections. Exact visual reordering, focus and gesture coordination remain to be specified and evaluated.

A preview or overview already open for a PR or Issue remains associated with that same source object when Today changes. If its prior cell no longer belongs to the selection, returning uses a supported current-context fallback under 0024 rather than substituting another object.

Confirmed private Repository revocation alone does not hide already saved local data; visibility follows the active-account and A-to-B boundary under 0019; keep the indication and supported time when known and stop synchronization for that Repository. A day change does not itself prove revocation or restoration of GitHub access.
Do not silently relabel a separately selected historical period as the new dynamic Today. Exact historical-period boundaries and behavior after a time-zone change remain open.
Make an applicable changed day, incomplete coverage or recovery limitation discoverable without relying solely on color or a transient visual cue.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Today uses the user's local calendar day, retaining earlier unfinished work and work completed on that day under 0007.
A new day does not make a prior-day completion alone qualify or delete the object from source history.
A changed day does not silently change Project or Repository scope or clear an explicit filter.
An open PR or Issue preview remains associated with the same object; missing new-day evidence does not become a confirmed empty selection.
Confirmed private Repository revocation preserves saved local information and its applicable limitation under 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Compact preview content by object type
nodes.description: Support inspection of a selected object from the overview with a compact, type-aware preview.

requirements.statement: Show the selected object's type and enough available identity and summary to distinguish it in its actual scope; include an available title or name, Repository context and source number where applicable. A short available source-text excerpt can assist identification; its absence does not establish that the source description is empty. Provide readable additional available detail beyond the originating cell under 0031. Opening and dismissal retain the same object's identity and origin.

Show the local Project name and supported member count and summary signals with their actual scope and coverage where available. Membership and source observations are distinct; a Project can include more than one Repository.

Show the supported Repository identity and available PR and Issue summaries in their observation context. An unavailable or changed source address does not identify another Repository merely because it has the same name.

Show supported Repository context, PR number, title and lifecycle, with available draft, CI, review and unresolved-thread signals. Retain CI, review assessment, requested reviews and thread counts as distinct observations; zero or unknown threads alone do not prove approval or a completed review. Counters do not require displaying individual check or thread content.

When known special or unclassified check outcomes are present, make their presence and available meaning or limitation discoverable through a non-color accessible path, without representing them as success. Exact source classification and presentation remain open under 0028.

Show supported Repository context, Issue number, title and open or closed state, with source closure reason when available. Do not assign PR-only review or CI status to an Issue or equate a closed Issue with successful completion. A blocker indication follows 0063 and its actual evidence.

Unknown, stale or incomplete fields do not become confirmed empty, zero or successful. A recently observed title or lifecycle does not establish equally recent review, CI, thread, related-object or counter data; keep applicable limitations available in preview or the accessible path to object overview.

After confirmed private Repository access revocation, saved local preview details, including saved source-derived names and counts, remain visible as last known with revocation indication and supported last update time when known. Preserve a local route to recovery or explicit deletion under 0019; local visibility does not restore source access and synchronization remains stopped. Do not invent a missing update time. Other account-change or offline disclosure cases remain open.
Offer an accessible way to open the same object locally and dismiss the preview under 0031; eligible source and sharing actions follow 0033. A source link does not guarantee renewed access.

Provide an accessible path to identify and open the selected object, inspect supported signals and their limitations, and distinguish them without color alone. Adapt presentation to available space and accessibility settings without making eight columns or an exact layout mandatory.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Preview identifies the selected object in its supported scope, provides readable additional available detail beyond the cell and offers local open and dismissal without retargeting it.
PR and Issue previews distinguish their supported state and type-specific signals without fabricating missing facts.
Project and Repository summaries retain their supported scope, coverage and observation limitations.

Saved preview details remain visible after confirmed private Repository access revocation with the indication and supported time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
The same object and applicable limitations are accessible without relying on color or long press alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Required Issue and PR description workflow
nodes.description: Make the selected Issue and PR description structure a requirement of the participating repository authoring process while keeping GitView usable for other source material.

requirements.statement: A new Issue description in the participating process requires Problem, Motivation, Expected outcome and References.
A new PR description in the participating process requires Problem, Motivation, Expected outcome, Changes, Validation and References.

Provide the agreed templates as inputs to the participating authoring process. The presence of a prefilled template or an agent instruction alone does not prove that the required sections were supplied, are meaningful or have been checked.

The participating process accounts for its supported creation paths, including person or agent paths that do not show the repository's web template. Exact coverage and the mechanism for detecting or correcting incomplete descriptions remain to be specified.

The process distinguishes a supported conforming new description from an incomplete or unverified one using an agreed rule. Structural conformance does not establish the truth of an authored motivation, outcome or validation claim. A source mechanism is not claimed to prevent or correct nonconformance until separately established.

GitView continues to show available existing, externally authored or differently structured Issues and PRs when eligible for display under 0019 and 0034. Preserve original text where available; inspection or compliance display does not rewrite the source description or fill sections automatically. Do not fabricate missing sections or hide an object solely because process compliance is missing or unknown. This does not decide a separately specified future editing flow.

An authored claim is distinct from independently observed source facts, review and CI. A linked Issue or a stated motivation does not prove the motive of a particular actor or the causal history of a change.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The participating process requires the selected Issue and PR section sets for new descriptions across its supported authoring paths.
A template or agent instruction alone is not treated as proof that sections were supplied or that every path is enforced.
Existing or external objects with missing or differently structured descriptions remain visible with their available original text when eligible under 0019; format alone does not hide them.
Structural conformance does not by itself establish an actor's motive, an achieved outcome, successful CI or independent validation.

nodes.title: GitView - Historical outcome selection
nodes.description: Let the operator inspect work associated with a supported historical outcome without confusing that event with the object's current state.

requirements.statement: Preserve the originating Project, supported event condition, object category, period and Repository basis when opening a historical outcome selection. Retain the supported period boundaries and time-zone interpretation when known; if unavailable, expose the limitation rather than inventing a different interval. Do not silently relabel that period as dynamic Today or replace it with an unrelated current-state filter.

A supported matching historical event must belong to the selected object and period. An object's current closed or merged state without sufficient event-time evidence does not establish that the event occurred in that period; missing history or unknown identity does not prove a non-match or complete empty selection.

Represent each source-confirmed matching PR or Issue at most once in the destination selection, even if it has several qualifying events. An event count and a count of distinct object cards are different units; a linked PR and Issue remain distinct objects.

When supported, display the object's latest observed lifecycle with its own observation context separately from the historical event condition. A reopened Issue can still match a prior supported closure event; its later current state alone does not reconstruct its earlier state or reason.

Keep explicit current-state filters distinct from the historical event condition. For the selected transition from a historical merged-PR counter, temporarily override a conflicting saved merged exclusion to show the counter result without rewriting the saved preference under 0047. Other transitions follow their signal origin and filter scope under 0092; exact filter hierarchy remains open. The previously selected historical merged-counter case concerns a counter whose originating scope includes merged PRs; a saved exclusion outside that origin does not narrow its destination. A counter defined inside a merged-excluding scope instead retains that origin scope.

Preserve actual source scope, observation times and incomplete event coverage. A supported partial selection is not a complete total or a confirmed zero for unobserved work. The originating metric and destination can have different observation contexts; do not fabricate equality or infer unseen objects.

Project historical graphs use current Project composition at evaluation under 0030 and 0047, with that basis identified. If Project membership changes while an existing historical selection is open, preserve its actual captured origin or disclose a limitation; do not silently claim an old captured scope is the new current composition.

Confirmed private Repository revocation alone does not hide already saved supported local historical information under 0019. Preserve its supported scope, time and applicable indication; do not claim newly current source access or fabricate missing event history. Visibility follows the active-account and A-to-B boundary under 0019.

Preserve valid originating context on return under 0024. If the originating Project or period cannot be supported, offer an appropriate limitation or fallback without silently substituting another Project or unrelated period.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A historical outcome selection preserves its originating Project, supported condition, category, period, supported boundaries and time-zone interpretation when known, and Repository basis rather than silently becoming Today.
A confirmed historical event remains distinct from the object's latest supported state; missing event evidence is not a confirmed non-match or complete zero.
Event counts and distinct object-card counts remain separate; the same confirmed object appears at most once in the destination.

For the selected counter whose originating scope includes merged PRs and whose saved merged exclusion is outside that scope: The selected historical merged-counter transition temporarily overrides a conflicting saved merged exclusion without rewriting the saved preference.
Incomplete coverage remains visible, and confirmed private Repository revocation alone does not hide saved supported local history under 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Project metric catalog and coverage
nodes.description: Make selected Project work, attention and period outcomes available as interpretable measurements and graphs when evidence supports them.

requirements.statement: A Project summary uses its applicable confirmed member Repositories; a shared Repository contributes within each Project while an asserted unique portfolio total follows 0029. Make the supported distinct member-Repository count and applicable category-specific coverage discoverable, such as an observed subset of a known member set; an unknown identity or denominator is not fabricated. Each value retains its actual scope, object category, unit, condition, supported observation time or period and coverage when available.

Distinguish supported open PRs, draft PRs and open Issues. A known draft PR is a subset of open PRs rather than additional independent work; an unknown draft flag is not silently non-draft. Current PR and Issue counts do not prove the number of independent tasks.

Make supported attention signals separately discoverable for failed CI, work awaiting review, changes requested, unresolved review threads and PRs affected by them, and Issues with supported open blockers. Keep each signal's actual unit, predicate and coverage distinct; a PR can contribute to several signals without becoming several PRs. Individual failed checks, affected PRs, affected Repositories and review threads are different units. Exact source predicates remain open; a review requirement or assignment to the operator is not automatically equivalent to awaiting review.

A green CI count, review assessment or zero visible unresolved threads does not alone establish merge readiness. A combined checks-and-review-passed selection requires a separately defined and accepted predicate; do not invent a ready count from unknown inputs.

Distinguish supported merged-PR outcomes and closed-Issue outcomes for an identified period. Make an Issue closure breakdown discoverable by source-supported reasons and retain unknown reason and incomplete coverage where applicable. A closure does not automatically establish a completed task; a current reason is not assigned to an earlier event without evidence. Distinguish event counts from distinct affected object counts, and do not assume reason groups sum to distinct Issues when one Issue can have multiple events. For PRs, the primary «Done» indicator denotes merged PRs; readiness to merge is a separate desired signal and must not be inferred from a merged count.

A confirmed merged PR can leave an unfinished-only current-work selection while remaining visible in unfiltered Today for the applicable local day under 0007. Its supported merge outcome can contribute to the applicable metric when subject, scope, period and evidence support it; one known outcome does not establish an exact total or complete coverage.

Provide graphs of selected supported summary metrics where historical evidence is sufficient under 0030. Identify current Project composition as the basis for its historical graphs under 0047; do not present it as the Project's historical membership. Missing history is a gap or incomplete scope, not an invented zero.

An actionable metric or signal retains its condition, actual Project or Repository scope, period and applicable coverage when opening a work selection. Event counts, check counts and distinct PR or Issue cards are not silently equated. The selected historical merged-counter transition uses the limited temporary filter override in 0047 and 0056 without rewriting saved preference.

Unknown, partial or stale source evidence retains its limitations and supported observation time when known; do not invent an unknown time. Successful metadata or one Repository data does not establish complete PR, Issue, review, CI or historical coverage for the whole Project.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository does not hide previously saved supported local measurements under 0019. Retain their actual scope, coverage, supported time when known and revocation indication; do not report them as newly refreshed. Visibility follows the active-account and A-to-B boundary under 0019.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Supported current work, attention and period outcomes remain distinguishable by Project or Repository scope, unit, condition, time and coverage.
Overlapping signals and different units are not silently added as separate PRs, Issues or independent tasks.
Graphs identify their current Project membership basis and do not turn missing historical evidence into a confirmed zero.
A closed Issue with unknown or non-completion reason is not automatically a completed task.

The selected merged-counter transition, whose origin includes merged PRs and whose saved exclusion is outside that origin, preserves its event scope and limited temporary filter override under 0047 and 0056.
Confirmed private Repository revocation alone does not hide saved supported local measurements under 0019 or make them newly current.
For the selected period, a discoverable Issue closure breakdown preserves supported reasons and the applicable unknown or incomplete coverage without inventing counts for unobserved work.

nodes.title: GitView - Connection and authorization outcomes
nodes.description: Let the operator understand whether a GitHub connection attempt succeeded, was cancelled, failed or remains unresolved without mistaking any one step for the whole outcome.

requirements.statement: Distinguish an in-progress authorization attempt, explicit cancellation, supported failure, confirmed connection and an indeterminate result. A callback, attempted authorization or locally supplied account label alone does not prove a connected source identity or current Repository access.

Report a new connection as confirmed only when supported successful authorization for that attempt and identity, the relevant source identity and locally required secure credential handling are established under 0019. If an outcome cannot be established, show the limitation and an applicable recovery route rather than inventing success or a definite failure.

Starting, cancelling or failing a new authorization does not by itself erase saved Projects or prior observations, prove source deletion, or replace an independently supported existing connection. A prior local connection does not alone prove current remote access.

A result from a cancelled, superseded or disconnected attempt cannot establish a new local connection, regardless of the outcome of any newer attempt. A separately initiated active attempt can establish its own outcome. Keep source and attempt context; local cancellation does not prove an independently completed source effect was undone. Actual identity and access evidence remain separate under 0036.

A connected account does not by itself establish a selected Repository, a saved Project or observed PR and Issue work. Partial discovery and uncertain setup outcomes retain their independent scope and recovery under 0022, 0045 and 0059.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of private Repository access for the relevant account leaves previously saved local data visible as last known with indication and supported update time when known under 0019. Stop synchronization for the affected Repository while revocation applies; the local view does not prove source access was restored.

Credentials and secret authorization-response material must not be exposed in ordinary diagnostics, sharing or user-facing errors. An error may describe an applicable recoverable outcome without displaying secret material.
Connection status, applicable failure or limitation and available continuation or recovery are understandable without relying on color or transient feedback alone.
