acceptance_criteria.statement: Authorization attempt outcomes remain distinguishable without reporting a callback or unverified account label as a confirmed connection.
Confirmed connection requires supported successful authorization for that attempt and identity, plus established required secure credential handling.
A cancelled, superseded or disconnected attempt does not establish a new local connection, regardless of the later attempt's outcome; source effects are not claimed undone without evidence.
Connection success does not by itself establish Project creation, Repository access or an observed work collection.

Confirmed private Repository revocation retains previously saved local data with indication and supported time when known; synchronization stops. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Connection limitations and available recovery are understandable without color or transient feedback alone, and credentials are not exposed.

nodes.title: GitView - Repository discovery and selection continuity
nodes.description: Let the operator find and choose Repositories without confusing incomplete discovery, pending choices or saved Project membership.

requirements.statement: Attribute results to their supported source account, query or selection scope, access context and coverage. Independently available choices remain usable when the result is partial, with the limitation visible. A sufficiently covered empty result establishes no match only within its stated scope; a failed or partial result does not establish source-wide absence.

Provide a way to find Repositories within available discovery and return to the broader available scope. A search over an incompletely observed subset does not prove there are no source matches. Matching, supported fields, ordering and whether search runs at the source remain open.

Use supported Repository identity under 0038 for selection and reconciliation. A name or address alone does not prove identity, and insufficient identity evidence remains unresolved rather than silently selecting or merging a different Repository.

A pending selection is distinct from a visible search subset and from saved Project membership. Search changes, refresh, pagination or temporary failure do not silently discard a confirmed pending choice. Provide a way to inspect and explicitly remove choices; selection alone neither creates a Project nor proves present source access under 0045. A choice retains its source account and intended operation; it is not silently relabeled or submitted under another account or setup intent. Exact retention and disclosure after an account change remain open.

Retain each response’s actual source, account and query context. A result for an earlier search is not presented as the current query’s complete result or as proof of access for a different connection. Make incomplete discovery and failures understandable; treatment of attempts for the same query remains a technical refinement.

Before a selected entry changes Project configuration, establish the identity and applicable access required by that operation. Missing evidence remains unresolved; a confirmed denial is not a valid prior grant. Keep independently supported outcomes distinct under 0045, without requiring batch selection or selecting a particular confirmation flow. Absence from partial discovery is not proof of denial, deletion or deselection; preserve a pending choice separately from its unresolved eligibility and offer an applicable retry or recovery when available.

When GitHub explicitly confirms access revocation for a private Repository for the relevant account, already saved local Repository data remains visible as last known with a revocation indication and supported update time when known; synchronization stops under 0019. An earlier in-flight response cannot silently restart sync or become a newly accepted update. Retained local visibility is not renewed source access or sufficient admission for a new operation. Other account-change disclosure beyond 0019 and treatment of unsaved pending data in other circumstances remain open.
Make search scope, available choices, incomplete discovery and applicable errors understandable without relying solely on color or transient feedback.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Discovery identifies its supported scope and distinguishes incomplete or failed results from confirmed empty results.
Selection retains supported Repository identity and survives a changed visible search subset without silently saving a Project.
Earlier responses are not presented as another query or connection, and insufficient identity or access remains unresolved.
Pending choice and operation intent are not silently relabeled or submitted under another account or intent.

Saved private data stays visible as last known after confirmed revocation with indication and supported time when known; sync stops, an earlier response does not silently restart it, and visibility does not authorize a new operation. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Search, available choices and discovery limitations are accessible without color or transient feedback alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Independent review attention conditions
nodes.description: Make review-related attention understandable without collapsing review requests, assessment and discussion into a single invented state.

requirements.statement: Keep supported outstanding review requests distinct from a source review assessment and from review-thread counts, each with its applicable source context, observation time when known and coverage. An unavailable request collection is not automatically a known empty collection.

Show a supported source review assessment without inferring approval from an absent request or zero unresolved threads. A source-reported review requirement, absence of reviews and unavailable assessment remain distinct where evidence supports them.

Preserve supported total and unresolved review-thread counts separately. A confirmed unresolved thread can support a positive attention signal even if remaining coverage is incomplete; zero observed unresolved threads does not establish absence when coverage or resolution evidence is incomplete. Outdated and resolved are separate source facts; a supported unresolved thread is not automatically treated as resolved or excluded from an all-unresolved count solely because it is outdated. Exact source mapping requires verification.

A source-reported request for changes and the existence of unresolved review threads are independent facts. A changes-requested assessment may remain meaningful even if supported thread evidence reports zero unresolved threads; do not convert either into approval or merge readiness.

For an applicable Project or Repository signal, distinguish the count of unresolved threads from the count of affected PRs. If counts are presented as comparable, retain the same explicitly stated PR population and period while preserving their distinct units and coverage. A single PR with several unresolved threads is not several distinct PRs. This does not impose that Project population on an individual PR overview.

Attribute review facts to their supported source time, revision and observation context when known. A later PR revision or a recently refreshed unrelated field does not silently make an older approval, request or thread count current for that revision.

Missing, partial, conflicting or stale evidence remains distinguishable from a confirmed healthy or zero result. A source-reported review requirement or assignment to the operator is not automatically the chosen definition of awaiting review.

Help the operator notice a review thread that has waited a long time for a reply to its latest message. The threshold, how to establish that a reply is awaited, applicable actor and evidence remain open; do not treat an old thread, a comment count or missing information alone as proof.

An actionable review or thread signal opens the corresponding supported work selection with its actual Project or Repository scope, condition, lifecycle population and applicable time or period under 0047. A count of threads is not automatically the count of resulting PR cards; incomplete selection coverage remains discoverable. Exact review or lifecycle predicates remain subject to their applicable specification.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository does not hide previously saved supported review facts under 0019; retain the applicable indication and supported time when known without claiming a fresh source result.
Review state and its limitations are understandable without relying on color alone. Exact glyphs and native presentation remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Review requests, assessment and total and unresolved thread counts remain distinct supported facts with their own applicable context and coverage.
Zero visible unresolved threads or zero outstanding requests alone does not establish approval, completed review or merge readiness.
A supported positive unresolved thread can be shown under incomplete coverage without claiming the full count or absence of others.
Thread counts and affected-PR counts are distinct units, and their navigation preserves the supported scope and condition.
Confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide previously saved supported review facts under 0019.
The intended long-wait signal concerns an awaited reply to the latest review-thread message; threshold and evidence are not silently invented.

nodes.title: GitView - Blocked Issue attention
nodes.description: Make supported blocked-Issue attention visible without confusing blocker links, source state or counts.

requirements.statement: Distinguish an Issue blocked by another Issue from an Issue that blocks another. A mention, parent-child relationship or ordinary link alone does not prove a blocking relationship.

A supported direct blocked-by relationship, open state of the affected Issue and open state of its blocker can establish a positive attention signal only when their observation contexts are sufficiently applicable to that claim. Differently timed or stale facts do not by themselves prove the relationship and both states were current together. Preserve supported last-known facts and their limitations without inventing a current positive.

Attribute the affected Issue to the selected Project or Repository scope. A supported blocker may be outside the originating Project without becoming a member of that Project merely through the relationship.

A blocked-Issue summary counts distinct affected open Issues, not blocker links or the number of blocking Issues. An Issue with two supported open blockers is still one affected Issue for this measurement; one Issue may also contribute to other independent signals.

Unobserved or incomplete blocker links, unavailable blocker state, uncertain identity or partial scope do not establish that an Issue is unblocked or that a Project has zero blocked Issues. Preserve the supported observation context and coverage and make the limitation discoverable.

An actionable blocked-Issue signal opens the distinct affected open Issues in its supported selection, not the blocker Issues merely because they are linked. Preserve the originating Project or Repository, supported condition and actual scope under 0047. Do not claim that a count of blocker links equals the count of Issue cards or that an incomplete destination is exhaustive.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository does not hide previously saved supported local facts under 0019; retain the indication and supported observation time when known. Local visibility does not prove a current source grant or current blocker state.
The applicable attention state, its uncertainty and available navigation remain understandable without relying solely on color.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A supported blocked-Issue attention count uses distinct affected open Issues, not the number of blocker links.
Supported blocked-by and blocking directions remain distinguishable, including when a blocker is outside the Project.
Unknown blocker state or incomplete relationship coverage is not treated as a confirmed unblocked Issue or a known zero.
An actionable signal preserves the originating scope and supported condition when opening its selection.
Confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide previously saved supported local information under 0019.
A closed affected Issue does not contribute to the blocked-work attention count even when its blocker is open; the blocker is assessed separately.

nodes.title: GitView - Project membership basis for historical metrics
nodes.description: Keep historical Project graphs interpretable when Project Repository membership changes.

requirements.statement: Recalculate a Project historical graph over the selected period using its actual current saved Repository composition under 0030. If membership cannot be established, report that limitation rather than invent a complete set. Missing source history or revoked access for a current member does not silently remove it from the basis; identify coverage and do not describe current members as the actual Project membership at past event times.

Keep each previously produced result attributable to the Repository set and observation context it actually used. When membership changes, do not relabel an earlier result as calculated for the new set. A current-member graph for the new composition must reassess its own input and coverage; missing history is incomplete or a gap, not zero.

A late result for an earlier membership basis cannot replace or be labeled as a separately selected new-basis result merely because it finished later. Retain each supported result's own metric, scope, period and observation context under 0026 and 0068.

A combined A-and-B value does not establish the A-only contribution without compatible per-member evidence. Values for A-and-B and A-and-C do not alone establish a same-scope trend or a change caused by source activity; keep the changed membership basis explicit.

A series that claims Project membership at a past time needs independently sufficient evidence of that local historical membership. GitHub Repository activity or today's Project configuration alone does not establish it. No membership-history store is required by this node.

A merge or closure event, historical state snapshot and distinct-object count have different evidence and units under 0030. A known event or current state alone does not prove a complete historical series; each bucket requires support for its stated metric and membership.

When GitHub explicitly confirms private Repository access revocation for the relevant account, supported previously saved graph values remain locally visible as last known with the revocation indication and supported observation times when known under 0019; synchronization stops. Missing attribution or lineage remains a visible limitation and does not justify inventing a scope, zero or current access. An in-flight response from before revocation is not accepted as a fresh update. Other account-change disclosure beyond 0019 and external sharing remain separate open questions.
Make membership basis, period, known coverage and changes understandable without color or transient feedback alone.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Historical Project graphs identify actual current saved Repository composition as their basis without claiming past membership; unestablished membership and missing input coverage remain limitations.
Membership changes do not silently relabel an earlier result or turn missing input history into zero.
An earlier late result does not replace a separately selected result for a different membership basis.

Saved supported graph values remain visible as last known after confirmed private Repository revocation with indication and supported time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Basis, scope and limitations remain accessible without color or transient feedback alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Metric history presentation and navigation
nodes.description: Let the operator inspect available Project metric history and move to supported related work without losing the measurement context.

requirements.statement: Make available supported metric history from its actual Project context. Preserve the selected Project, measurement, period and source scope; do not silently substitute another Project that shares a Repository.

Identify the supported series subject, unit, condition, period, observation context and coverage. When values are bucketed, make their supported boundaries and time-zone interpretation discoverable when known; unknown context remains a limitation. A Project historical graph identifies current Project membership as its basis under 0030 and 0047; it does not claim to reconstruct Project membership at the historical time.

If Project membership changes while a graph remains open, preserve and identify the basis of the existing graph without calling it the new current composition. Recalculate against the newly current membership when supported or expose the applicable limitation; exact timing remains open.

Keep a confirmed zero distinguishable from unobserved history and incomplete coverage in both visual and accessible representations. Do not fabricate a complete total, an exact missing count or a source event from a gap.

If an available historical outcome offers navigation to related work, preserve its supported event condition, object type, period boundaries and time-zone interpretation when known, Repository basis and Project origin under 0056. When that selection cannot be supported, expose the limitation rather than silently switching to Today or a different period.

Distinguish event counts, distinct PR or Issue counts, check counts and the number of resulting object cards. One object can correspond to more than one historical event; a point and destination observed at different times do not automatically have equal counts. A later selection with the same count is not the exact original contributor set unless identity evidence supports that claim; otherwise preserve its own observation context and coverage.

The selected historical merged-PR counter transition temporarily overrides a conflicting saved merged exclusion under 0047 and 0056 without rewriting the saved preference. Other signal transitions follow the actual origin filter context under 0092: filters within that scope apply; unrelated filters outside it do not narrow the result. Exact filter hierarchy, controls and return behavior remain open.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of a private Repository does not hide a previously saved supported local series under 0019. Retain its actual scope, supported time when known, coverage and applicable indication; do not present it as newly current. Visibility follows the active-account and A-to-B boundary under 0019.

Returning from metric history or its selection preserves valid originating Project context under 0024. Displaying or leaving history does not itself change source objects, membership or saved filter preferences.
Provide a way to inspect supported values, scope, period, coverage and available navigation without relying solely on color, chart position or a particular gesture under 0032.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Available metric history preserves its originating Project, supported measurement and selected period.
Series scope, unit, current-membership basis and applicable coverage are distinguishable; an unobserved gap is not presented as a confirmed zero.
An actionable historical outcome preserves its supported origin and event condition or exposes a limitation rather than silently becoming Today.
Event or check counts are not silently equated with distinct PR or Issue card counts.

For the selected merged counter whose origin includes merged PRs and whose saved exclusion is outside that origin, the transition preserves the limited temporary filter override without rewriting the saved preference.
Supported history and limitations are accessible without reliance solely on color, chart position or a particular gesture.

nodes.title: GitView - Project overview order and position
nodes.description: Keep Projects identifiable and the overview position understandable across updates and navigation.

requirements.statement: Represent each supported saved Project by its identity, not a Repository name or cell position. A source refresh, Repository rename or membership edit does not by itself create a different Project. An unknown setup result does not itself prove that a Project was saved.

Ordinary source refresh or density changes do not themselves reorder existing Projects; changing counts is not automatically an urgency sort. Adding or removing a Project does not duplicate or reidentify others. This does not establish an initial sort rule.

On return from a Project, maintain its identity as a position or focus anchor when present and available under 0024 and 0073. The same Project may occupy a different cell or viewport coordinate after reflow.

If an anchor is unavailable, preserve the actual context and use a supported fallback without presenting a different Project as the original. An incomplete collection read does not prove the missing Project was deleted or that a proposed fallback is its definitive successor.

If Projects are readable but ordering information is unavailable or inconsistent, preserve access to supported Projects and make the ordering limitation discoverable. Do not claim the earlier order was restored or infer an empty collection solely from missing order information. The fallback ordering rule remains open.
Preserve a coherent active gesture or accessible interaction where feasible as the collection changes. The exact native transition and timing remain open under 0073.

On GitHub-confirmed access revocation for a private Repository for the relevant account, previously saved Project name and supported Repository data remain visible and accessible as last known with indication and supported update time when known under 0019; do not defer that indication until a gesture or reordering finishes. Synchronization of the affected Repository stops while revocation applies; a late response cannot silently restore access or become a newly accepted update. Other independently eligible Repositories may continue synchronizing.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Existing Projects retain supported identity and stable relative order through ordinary refresh or density changes.
Returning to a present Project restores a meaningful identity anchor without treating its old position as identity.
A missing anchor or unavailable order is communicated without fabricating deletion or substituting another Project.

Saved Project and affected Repository details remain visible as last known after GitHub-confirmed private Repository revocation for the relevant account with indication and supported update time when known; synchronization stops while revocation applies. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Overview navigation and its limitations remain accessible without depending only on gesture or color.

nodes.title: GitView - Accessible focus during overview updates
nodes.description: Preserve meaningful accessible navigation when overview content, scope or data status changes.

requirements.statement: Keep the inspected object's supported identity and scope distinct from a cell position, reused name or Repository-local number. If it remains in the collection after reorder or density change, maintain or restore an accessible path to that same object where feasible.

When selection evidence becomes uncertain, keep an available object inspectable through the uncertain selection or an equivalent path under 0042, subject to applicable disclosure context. Confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide saved data under 0019; other account-change disclosure beyond the selected A-to-B rule in 0019 remains open. Disclose uncertainty rather than announcing a confirmed match or exclusion solely from missing evidence.

If the object no longer belongs to the active collection, use an appropriate surviving anchor or collection-state fallback under 0024 without describing a different object as the original. An already open preview retains its identity under 0031; apply fallback on return.

Make relevant refresh failure, incomplete coverage and Today period changes discoverable in the accessible context or a status route without relying only on transient feedback or color. A completed request is not proof of complete coverage.

Avoid disruptive changes while the operator is actively inspecting or navigating when a coherent presentation is possible; subsequently reconcile the applicable collection without indefinite deferral. No exact animation or announcement timing is selected.

On confirmed private Repository revocation, keep saved content accessible with a revocation indication and supported update time when known under 0019, without waiting for a reordered collection. Stop synchronization and keep recovery or explicit local deletion reachable.

A retained focus anchor does not prove that a newly active source account has access. Do not silently attribute it to another object. Other local disclosure after account change beyond the selected A-to-B rule remains open under 0019; confirmed revocation retains its selected visibility.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Reordering or reflow does not substitute an object for another at the previous position.
Uncertain selection and incomplete coverage remain accessible without inventing exclusions or counts.
When the focused object leaves the collection, a supported fallback does not misidentify another object as it.
Confirmed revocation leaves saved content accessible with the indication and supported update time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Relevant errors and period changes remain discoverable without requiring transient feedback or color.

nodes.title: GitView - Overview levels and scope transitions
nodes.description: Let the operator move from an overview of Projects into the relevant Repository or work scope without losing identity or navigation context.

requirements.statement: A Project with one Repository reaches that Repository's work without a redundant intermediate Repository screen. Project and Repository remain distinct, with their supported identities and context available.

A Project with several Repositories allows the operator to inspect its members and reach the work of each. Repositories can come from different GitHub organizations; organization is metadata, not an implicit Project boundary.

An actionable Project summary signal can open its corresponding work across the applicable member scope without requiring a Repository-by-Repository detour. Preserve the originating Project, signal condition, applicable period and each object supported Repository context; incomplete evidence does not establish an exhaustive selection. For the selected historical merged-PR counter transition, apply the temporary conflicting merged-filter override under 0047 without rewriting the saved preference; other signals follow their own originating filter context under 0092. The previously selected historical merged-counter case concerns a counter whose originating scope includes merged PRs; a saved exclusion outside that origin does not narrow its destination. A counter defined inside a merged-excluding scope instead retains that origin scope.

Ordinary entry to a multi-Repository Project opens its Project-wide PR and Issue grid across the applicable member scope; the Repository list is available in Project settings. Preserve member inspection, per-Repository work and actionable signal routes.

Pinch or an accessible equivalent changes density in discrete steps within the current scope under 0035. On reaching the maximum cell size, pinch enters the corresponding next level when the intended target is unambiguous under 0014; this intentional transition preserves the selected target and its context.
A Repository shared by several Projects retains the actual Project origin from which it was opened. The same name or position does not justify silently substituting another Project or Repository.

Confirmed GitHub revocation alone does not hide an already saved local Project, member or supported work under 0019. Present the applicable revocation indication and supported time when known without claiming restored source access; account isolation and external handoff remain separate questions.

Preserve valid originating scope, applicable period, filters and density on return where possible under 0024. If an origin or selected object is no longer supported, provide a meaningful applicable fallback without silently representing a different Project as the original.
The operator can navigate and inspect applicable Projects, members and work without relying solely on pinch, color or a precise tiny target under 0032.

The owner envisages further pinch out from Today reaching the daily work-intensity calendar under 0018; this is an outward transition and does not alter the maximum-cell-size rule for zooming in. Exact interaction and first-version inclusion remain open.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A single-Repository Project reaches its work without a redundant intermediate Repository screen while retaining both identities.
A multi-Repository Project permits member inspection and a route to each member's work; organizations do not silently redefine Project membership.
An actionable Project signal reaches its corresponding work across the applicable scope without an individual Repository detour and retains its supported condition and source context.
Before the boundary, density changes preserve scope and filters; an intentional boundary transition and return preserve the intended target and applicable context.
Confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide already saved local Project or member information under 0019.
Ordinary entry to a multi-Repository Project opens its Project-wide work grid, with its member list available in Project settings.

nodes.title: GitView - Grid interaction and interruption
nodes.description: Keep scrolling, density changes, static preview and explicit navigation understandable and bound to the intended object.

requirements.statement: An ordinary recognized scroll moves the collection without also opening an object or activating its preview solely from that interaction.

Pinch changes density through discrete steps within the current scope; on reaching the maximum cell-size boundary it triggers a transition to the intended next level under 0014. Grid width and maximum cell size in points determine the boundary. A pinch recognized while a press is pending does not also activate that pending preview; an ambiguous target is not silently substituted.

Preserve a meaningful position or supported object identity through density reflow where feasible; an old cell coordinate or another object with the same local number is not identity. If no unambiguous object is available, do not invent a selection; use a supported fallback under 0024.

A recognized long press on an eligible object presents that same object's static preview under 0031. Movement over another cell does not alone retarget it or imply the future sliding mode. Explicit opening and dismissal retain the established object identity.

Cancellation of an unfinished interaction leaves a coherent current overview without claiming that an object was opened or another action committed. An independently completed action is not retroactively undone solely by a later interruption.

Refresh, day boundary or Project edit may independently alter the selection while an interaction is in progress. Do not attribute that change to pinch alone or silently retarget a pending action to a different object at the old coordinate. A touch begun without an eligible object does not select a newly appearing cell merely because reflow places it under that touch. On confirmed private Repository revocation, retain supported saved cells with indication and time when known and stop synchronization under 0019 without waiting for gesture completion.
Provide accessible paths to change density, invoke and dismiss preview, and open an object without requiring pinch, long press, a timed gesture or color alone under 0032 and 0073.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Scroll, density change, static preview and explicit object opening have distinguishable outcomes without substituting another object.
An in-scope pinch preserves the applicable Project, Repository scope, period and filters.
Cancellation or independent collection changes do not silently open or retarget a different object.

Saved cells remain visible after confirmed private Repository revocation with indication and supported time when known; synchronization stops. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Density changes, preview and object opening have accessible alternatives to pinch, long press and color alone.
Pinch moves through discrete detail levels and enters the intended next level at the maximum cell-size boundary when the target is unambiguous under 0014.

nodes.title: GitView - Issue discussion counts and latest comment time
nodes.description: Make Issue comment and participant counts and the time of the latest comment interpretable with their actual scope and evidence.

requirements.statement: Keep comment count, participant count and latest-comment time distinct with their supported Issue identity, source, population, scope and observation context. Issue comments are not PR review threads, and comment count does not by itself establish participant count.

An observed current population is not automatically a complete history of deleted, hidden or otherwise unobserved discussion. A source-provided aggregate can support a count only when its documented population, scope, time and available evidence match that claim. A partial enumerated subset is not added to an aggregate as if independently disjoint.

Preserve the actual source-supported meaning of a participant count; do not present a narrower source population as every person, agent or actor without evidence of equivalence. Whether a separate distinct comment-author count is useful remains open.

Unknown, unavailable or incomplete discussion data is not a confirmed zero. Sufficient evidence for one count does not by itself establish the other count or a latest-comment time; retain each available observation and its own limitation.

An exact latest-comment time is the maximum supported comment creation instant in the stated sufficiently covered population, not the Issue's update time, GitView observation time or the time an older comment was edited. A maximum observed in an incomplete subset is not automatically the latest in the whole Issue and retains its subset limitation.
A new title or unrelated Issue update does not refresh an earlier discussion count or latest-comment time. Retain each supported value's own time and context under 0044 and 0026.

When GitHub explicitly confirms private Repository access revocation for the relevant account, previously saved discussion values remain locally visible as last known with revocation indication and supported update time when known; synchronization stops under 0019. No live source access is implied, and an unknown time is not invented.

Make selected counts and latest-comment time, their distinct meanings, applicable limitations and known absence versus unknown understandable to assistive technology and without color or transient feedback alone.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Issue comments, participants and latest-comment time retain distinct units, supported context and limitations.
Missing or incomplete evidence for one value is not silently turned into zero or inferred from another value.
Exact latest-comment time is the supported maximum creation instant in its sufficiently covered population, distinguished from Issue update, observation and later comment edit times.

Saved discussion values remain visible after confirmed private Repository revocation with indication and supported update time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Counts, latest-comment time, known absence and uncertainty remain accessible without color or transient feedback alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Issue links, hierarchy and partial observations
nodes.description: Preserve the meaning, direction and limitations of selected Issue links and direct-child counts without treating an observed link as an actor's motive.

requirements.statement: Preserve supported PR mentions, closing references, parent, direct child, blocked-by and blocking connections as distinct directional source facts. A mention does not alone prove a closing reference, completion, actor's motive or causal history. The same confirmed target can retain multiple supported link meanings without becoming multiple target identities under 0039.

Associate each link with supported source and target identity, type, direction, scope, observation time and coverage when known. Absence from a partial or inaccessible collection is not confirmed absence; a refreshed title does not automatically refresh previously observed links.

Count supported distinct direct sub-Issues and their closed subset separately. A grandchild is not a direct child solely through its parent; a closed child is not necessarily completed work. Evaluate evidence for the total and closed subset separately. A complete list of distinct direct children can establish total even when one child's state is unknown, but cannot by itself establish an exact closed count. An independently supported source aggregate may establish a count only for the compatible population, state, access and time it actually covers. Incomplete evidence for a particular count is not an exact total or zero.
A supported blocked-by link and the linked Issue's current lifecycle are separate facts. A link alone does not prove a blocker is currently open; preserve uncertain coverage under 0063.

A supported linked object retains its own Repository identity and originating context. Opening it does not silently add its Repository to the originating Project or substitute a same-number object in another Repository. Returning preserves the valid origin under 0024; source handoff follows 0033.

If an observed link changes or disappears, retain its supported observation context; do not present an earlier link as current without sufficient evidence. A link change does not by itself prove that either object was deleted or change Project membership.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of private Repository access for the relevant account does not hide already saved local Issue, linked-object or relationship data under 0019. Show supported saved information as last known with revocation indication and supported update time when known; stop syncing the affected Repository. Local visibility does not restore source access. Other account-change disclosure conditions remain open.
Make supported link meaning, direction, partial coverage and available navigation understandable without relying only on color or a transient cue.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Supported Issue links retain type, direction, identities and their observation limitations without asserting motive or completion.
Direct-child totals do not include grandchildren by implication or convert closed counts into completion.
Partial coverage is not treated as a confirmed empty or complete relationship set.
Navigating to a supported linked target does not silently change Project membership or substitute another object.

Saved supported linked data stays visible after confirmed private Repository revocation with indication and supported time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Temporal context of Today and filter evidence
nodes.description: Preserve the meaning of Today inclusion and active filters when their source observations refer to different times or revisions.

requirements.statement: Dynamic Today follows the user's applicable current local calendar day under 0049. A completed object does not qualify for a new day solely because it completed on the previous day; other independently applicable inclusion conditions may qualify it.

Preserve each supported fact's object, source scope, event time where applicable and observation time when supported, plus revision where applicable and coverage. The time an observation was retrieved is not automatically the time a source event occurred; refreshing one field does not refresh omitted fields.

Today inclusion, current lifecycle and each active filter are separate claims. A supported inclusion alternative can establish base eligibility without proving a separate active filter. An unknown required filter remains uncertain unless another independently applicable false required condition decides exclusion under 0027.

Do not represent an earlier observation as confirmed for a later requested context solely because it was locally read, another field refreshed or no later event is known. Retain its supported last-known context and expose applicable uncertainty; source-specific evidence for current applicability remains open rather than assuming a universal time-to-live or permanent uncertainty.

A source-confirmed newer PR revision does not automatically inherit checks or review observations from an older revision. Preserve their original context and use independently supported evidence when evaluating the current revision under 0028.

Facts observed at different times are not presented as one confirmed simultaneous snapshot without sufficient supporting evidence. Preserving a selected filter or period does not establish complete source coverage.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of private Repository access for the relevant account does not hide supported saved facts and values; retain them as last known with indication and supported time when known under 0019, and stop synchronization. A late earlier response does not restore access or become a newly accepted update.
Make active filters, uncertainty, relevant observation context and incomplete coverage discoverable without relying solely on color or transient feedback.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Today retains the selected local-day behavior and does not treat yesterday's completion alone as today's work.
Inclusion, active filter inputs and displayed lifecycle retain their own supported context and limitations.
Old revision checks and mixed-time observations do not silently become confirmed current or simultaneous facts.

Confirmed private Repository revocation retains supported saved values with indication and supported time when known; synchronization stops. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Filter state and uncertainty are discoverable without color or transient feedback alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Work scope as Project membership changes
nodes.description: Preserve the operator's actual Project or Repository work scope as Project membership changes.

requirements.statement: Distinguish a Project-wide work selection from an explicitly selected Repository within a Project, even if the Project currently has only one member. Density or source refresh does not silently change the chosen scope.

When a saved membership edit adds Repository B to Project P, an existing P-wide selection reevaluates against P's confirmed new member set while retaining the valid Project, period, filters and density. Prior complete observations for A alone do not establish B's work or complete coverage for A and B under 0044.

When the operator is viewing explicitly selected Repository A within P, adding B does not silently widen the selection to B. If A is removed from P, do not silently substitute B or another Project; identify the changed origin and offer a supported route under 0024.

A saved membership removal changes the Project-wide scope without proving source deletion or erasing independently retained data. Another Project containing the same Repository retains its own membership and observation context.

A pending, cancelled before submission, failed or indeterminate edit is not itself proof of a new saved membership. An independently confirmed edit can nevertheless change the actual Project; if the current configuration cannot be reconciled, keep it uncertain rather than claiming complete coverage for either presumed member set under 0025.

An already open preview or object that remains available under the applicable context stays available with its supported identity through a membership edit; it does not silently become a different object. On dismissal or return restore the actual valid in-session origin or explain its limitation under 0024 and 0031, without inventing a new intermediate route. This preserves the actual origin without changing the selected Project-wide ordinary entry for a later fresh entry.

Confirmed GitHub revocation of private Repository access for the relevant account does not hide already saved local Project or Repository information under 0019. Keep its indication and supported update time when known, stop syncing the affected Repository and do not claim renewed access.
Make scope changes, incomplete coverage and applicable recovery routes discoverable without relying only on color or transient feedback.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Project-wide and explicitly Repository-scoped selections preserve their distinct intent as membership changes.
A confirmed membership change does not silently clear the valid Project, period or filters or reuse prior coverage for an unobserved member.
Removed or uncertain origin does not silently substitute another Repository or Project or imply source deletion.

An open object's identity is retained through membership changes; saved private data remains visible after confirmed revocation under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Scope limitations and recovery are understandable without color or transient feedback alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Signal-origin selection and explicit filter changes
nodes.description: Preserve the meaning of an actionable summary signal when the operator opens and navigates its associated work selection.

requirements.statement: Retain the supported originating Project and, for a Repository-specific signal, the actual Repository identity, condition, unit, period, membership basis, coverage and observation time when known. The origin does not prove that every contributing object has been loaded or that its observation is current.

Open the supported corresponding work selection with its actual condition and scope. If the condition, source identity or period cannot be represented with available evidence, make the limitation discoverable instead of silently substituting Today, a different Project or unrelated filter.

Distinguish the signal's measurement unit from the destination's distinct PR or Issue cards. A count of checks, review threads or events is not automatically the number of PR or Issue cards; the same object is not duplicated merely because multiple events qualify.

For the selected transition from a historical merged-PR counter, temporarily override a conflicting saved merged exclusion under 0047 and 0056 to show the counter result without rewriting the saved preference. Other transitions follow their actual origin context, not an assumed universal override.

If the operator explicitly changes or clears an active condition, do not continue to describe every displayed object as matching the original condition. Such a change does not alter source objects or rewrite the earlier observed signal; persistence of ordinary user filters remains governed by 0007 and its own supported save outcome.

Keep the origin measurement and destination's actual observation time, source scope and coverage attributable to each. If refresh or incomplete source evidence yields a different count or partial selection, do not fabricate equality, a missing object count or a confirmed empty result.

A confirmed membership, source identity or day change may require reevaluating the applicable selection. Do not silently transfer an earlier observation to a different Project, Repository or historical period; use the relevant supported context or disclose a limitation under 0024 and 0056.

Confirmed private Repository revocation does not hide already saved supported local origin details, counts or objects under 0019. Preserve their supported scope and time when known and the applicable indication; local visibility is not a fresh source grant.
Return to the actual valid originating surface and context under 0024. A source error or absent evidence does not prove that another Project is the correct replacement.
Make the applicable signal meaning, active condition, scope, limitation and available navigation understandable without relying solely on color or a particular gesture.

When the originating signal belongs to a filtered scope, preserve that scope and its applicable filters in the destination. A signal outside a filter context opens its corresponding selection without being narrowed by that unrelated filter. Preserve actual access, Project, period and coverage; this does not rewrite a saved preference or imply full source coverage. The detailed hierarchy, inheritance and controls remain open. The previously selected historical merged-counter case concerns a counter whose originating scope includes merged PRs; a saved exclusion outside that origin does not narrow its destination. A counter defined inside a merged-excluding scope instead retains that origin scope.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An actionable signal preserves its supported origin, condition, scope, unit and period when opening its corresponding work selection, or exposes a limitation.
Signal measurement units are not silently equated with counts of distinct destination cards.

For the selected counter whose originating scope includes merged PRs and whose saved merged exclusion is outside that scope: The selected historical merged-counter transition temporarily overrides the conflicting saved merged exclusion without rewriting the saved preference.
An explicitly changed or cleared condition is not still presented as applying to every displayed object.
Incomplete observations, changed context or confirmed private Repository revocation do not silently substitute another Project or invent fresh source data.
A signal from a filtered scope retains its applicable filter context; an unrelated filter outside the signal context does not narrow its destination or rewrite saved preferences.

nodes.title: GitView - Preview availability and changing observations
nodes.description: Keep the selected object's preview useful and correctly attributed as data availability and source observations change.

requirements.statement: Open a preview of already available supported local data where eligible for local display under 0019 without waiting for a network response. Identify the same selected object and preserve its origin; unavailable data is not invented or treated as confirmed zero.

Each fact keeps its supported object, source, time, revision where relevant and limitations. A new title does not make an older review or CI observation current for a newer PR revision. A partial refresh updates only fields the observation actually supports.

A late observation for an earlier preview must not be rendered as belonging to a different selected object. Reopening an object does not alone prove the earlier observation is current or eligible for the new view; apply its original context and applicable access and ordering rules before showing it.
Dismissing a preview does not implicitly open it again when an observation arrives or prove that an underlying request was cancelled. Return and explicit opening follow 0031 and 0024.

An explicitly cancelled or invalidated pending local open does not later navigate into an object or disrupt a newer context. Closing the preview as part of a successfully accepted open is not itself evidence of cancellation.

If private Repository revocation is confirmed before or while preview is open, keep previously saved local details visible with revocation indication and supported time when known; stop synchronization under 0019. An earlier in-flight response does not silently restore source access or become a newly accepted update. Recovery or explicit local deletion remains reachable.

Opening locally, opening the source and sharing are distinct actions. A supported source link identifies the intended object and does not by itself establish current access or create a GitHub URL for a local Project under 0033.

Provide discoverable ways to invoke and dismiss the preview of the same object without long press. Available identity, state, limitations and actions are accessible without relying on color; direct object open is distinct from access to preview under 0032.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Supported local preview information eligible for display is available without waiting for a network response and remains attributed to the selected object.
Late or partial observations do not silently retarget a preview, reopen a dismissed preview or make unsupported fields current.

Confirmed private Repository revocation leaves saved details visible with indication and supported update time when known; synchronization stops. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Local open, source handoff and sharing remain distinct. Preview invocation, dismissal, identity and limitations have accessible paths without long press or color alone.

nodes.title: GitView - Attention to lengthy review discussions
nodes.description: Help the operator notice review discussions that may need attention, including threads waiting a long time for a response, without leaving the work overview.

requirements.statement: Help the operator notice a review thread that has waited a long time for a reply to its latest message. Show such a signal when its predicate and the necessary evidence are established; the duration threshold, applicable actor and how waiting for a reply is established remain open.

Describe the actual meaning and scope of an available signal so the operator can understand why it needs attention. Unknown or incomplete information is not presented as proof that no discussion needs attention.

If counts are shown, distinguish the number of qualifying review threads from the number of affected PRs; several threads on one PR do not make several PRs. Individual thread content is not required in GitView.
An actionable signal leads to the corresponding work in its Project or Repository context, with any applicable limitation. The operator can reach the original GitHub object.

After GitHub confirms private Repository access revocation, keep saved review information visible as last known with its revocation indication and supported update time when known; stop synchronization and preserve access recovery or explicit local deletion under 0019.
Make the signal meaning, applicable limitations and available navigation understandable without relying solely on color or transient feedback.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The selected attention need concerns a long wait for a reply to the latest review-thread message; its predicate, threshold and evidence are not invented.
An available signal has an understandable meaning and scope, and unknown information is not presented as a confirmed absence.
Thread counts and affected PR counts remain distinguishable, and actionable navigation keeps the applicable scope.

Saved private review information remains visible after confirmed access revocation with its indication and supported update time when known under 0019. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
Signal meaning and available actions do not rely solely on color or transient feedback.
The long-wait signal concerns a reply awaited to the latest review-thread message; its threshold and evidence remain to be specified.

nodes.title: GitView - Work object identity in Today
nodes.description: Preserve distinct source-supported PR and Issue identities when constructing a Today work selection from potentially overlapping or incomplete observations.

requirements.statement: Before treating an observation as a PR or Issue, use supported object-type evidence. An untyped or identity-ambiguous representation remains unresolved; do not silently classify it or fabricate a confirmed match, exclusion or exact population count.

Multiple source observations or inclusion conditions for a source-confirmed same PR or Issue do not create multiple cells for that object in the same selection. An Issues-source representation confirmed as a PR is not an additional independent Issue under 0039. The same Repository can belong to different Projects; its eligible object can appear once in each applicable Project selection, without changing membership or globally suppressing it across Projects.

A separately identified Issue and PR remain distinct even when linked or describing related work. Same-number PRs or Issues in different Repositories do not become one object. A link is not proof of motive or of independent task count.

Preserve identifier type, source instance and Repository context. Do not equate or interchange source representation identifiers solely because their numbers, names or addresses resemble one another. Repository identity follows 0038; associating work-object representations requires its own supported evidence under 0039, and the source-specific association method remains open.

Keep supported lifecycle, event time, observation time, scope and coverage distinct per fact. Missing, unrecognized, conflicting or omitted facts are not invented from another field or from retrieval time. A closed PR is not automatically merged; a PR closure is not an Issue closure.

An unresolved representation or missing type evidence can limit the completeness of a materialized work selection. Independently supported counts retain their own scope and evidence; a count alone does not create object identities or establish that all cards are present under 0044.

On GitHub-confirmed private Repository revocation for the relevant account, previously saved supported work remains visible locally as last known with revocation indication and supported time when known under 0019; synchronization stops. An earlier response does not silently become a fresh update or restore access. Other account-change disclosure beyond the selected A-to-B rule in 0019 remains open.
Make known object type, identity context and applicable uncertainty understandable without relying only on color or a transient cue.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Confirmed PRs and Issues retain supported identity and type; unresolved representations are not silently classified.
A source-confirmed PR represented through an Issues source is not counted as a separate Issue, and an independently linked Issue remains distinct.
Equal local numbers or display names do not merge different Repository objects or substitute unsupported source identifiers.
Missing source facts do not become a fabricated lifecycle transition, event time or complete work population.

Saved supported work remains visible after confirmed private Repository revocation with indication and supported time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.

nodes.title: GitView - Completed work and PR review stage
nodes.description: Preserve the requested view of what is ready while distinguishing completed outcomes from review stage and independently supported attention signals.

requirements.statement: For PRs, the primary «Done» indicator means PRs already merged. Show readiness to merge separately; its product predicate, source evidence and applicability remain to be defined. A merged outcome is not the same as a PR awaiting merge, and one source field does not by itself establish the separate readiness signal.

Present a supported merged PR as merged and a PR closed without merge accordingly. Present an Issue as closed with its supported reason when available; an unknown or non-completion reason does not automatically establish a successfully completed task. Current lifecycle and an event during a selected period are distinct facts under 0039, 0041 and 0057.

Without an applicable saved exclusion, an eligible PR in the selected Project with a supported merge today remains the same object in unfiltered Today while an explicitly unfinished-only selection can hide it under 0027. A filter does not modify the source object or erase the supported outcome.

Preserve applicable PR lifecycle, draft status, review assessment, requests, unresolved threads and CI as independently supported facts with their actual observation context. Non-draft, green CI, approval or zero visible threads alone does not prove an assigned reviewer, completed review or merge eligibility. A combination of these signals also does not establish merge eligibility without a separately defined applicable predicate and sufficient source evidence.

If a future open non-draft PR filter is selected, name and explain its actual predicate; it must not be called merge-ready or treated as a review request solely from that status. The predecessor's proposed filter remains a candidate, not a mandatory first-version feature.

Missing, stale, incompatible or incomplete evidence is not a confirmed ready state, completed outcome, exact count or absence. An independently supported lifecycle outcome may remain visible with its own context even when a review or CI signal is unknown.

If an applicable signal or count opens work, retain its condition, scope, time and coverage under 0047 and 0092. Different counts or observations do not automatically identify the same PR population, and navigation does not modify GitHub.

After confirmed GitHub revocation of private Repository access for the relevant account, supported saved facts remain visible as last known with indication and supported update time when known under 0019; synchronization stops and a late old response does not restore current access.
Supported outcomes, independent signals and their limitations are understandable without relying on color or transient feedback alone.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The need to see ready work remains explicit without asserting that an unselected predicate resolves it.
Supported completed outcomes, PR draft status, review signals and CI retain distinct meanings and context.
Unfiltered Today preserves eligible same-day merged PRs unless the operator's applicable saved filter excludes them.
Unknown or incomplete evidence does not become a confirmed ready state, completed outcome or exact count.

Saved supported facts remain visible after confirmed private Repository revocation with indication and supported time when known. Visibility and local access follow the active-account and A-to-B boundary in 0019.
For PRs the primary «Done» indicator means merged; readiness to merge is presented separately under a separately defined predicate and supported evidence.
